**Tafsir Surat al-Hajj**
*[It is Meccan]* [[Addition from MS T.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His servants to be mindful of Him (taqwa), and informing them of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, its convulsions, and its conditions that they will face: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing.﴾ The commentators (mufassirun) have differed concerning the convulsion of the Hour: Is it after people rise from their graves on the Day of their resurrection and proceed to the plains of Judgment? Or is it a reference to the convulsion of the earth before people rise from their tombs? As Allah says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, and the earth discharges its burdens﴾ [al-Zalzalah 99:1-2]. And He says: ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow. So on that Day the Occurrence will occur﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:14-15]. And He says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with convulsion, and the mountains are broken into dust, and they become scattered dust﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:4-6].

Some said: This convulsion will occur at the end of the life of this world and at the beginning of the conditions of the Hour.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: "Before the Hour."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, and he mentioned it. He said: It was also related from al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim, and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, something similar.

Abu Kudaynah said, from 'Ata', from 'Amir al-Sha'bi: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: "This is in the world, before the Day of Resurrection."

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir has cited the basis (musnad) of those who held this view in the hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur), through the narration of Isma'il ibn Rafi', judge of the people of Madinah, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet, and gave it to Israfil. He places it at his mouth, gazing with his eyes toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded."

Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Trumpet?"

He said: "A horn."

He said: "What is it like?"

He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown. The first is the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza'), the second is the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds (nafkhat al-qiyam li-Rabb al-'alamin). Allah will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: 'Blow the blast of terror.' So the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. He will command him, and he will prolong it and extend it without pause. This is what Allah, exalted is He, refers to: ﴿They await but one shout; it will have no respite﴾ [Sad 38:15]. Then Allah will set the mountains moving, and they will become like mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people in a violent shaking. This is what Allah, exalted is He, refers to: ﴿On the Day the quaking one will quake, followed by the following. Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:6-8]. The earth will be like a ship tossed in the sea, struck by the waves, tilting with its people, and like a lamp suspended from the Throne, swayed by the winds.

Then people will spread out over its surface, so nursing mothers will be distracted and pregnant women will give birth. Children will turn gray, and the devils will flee in terror until they reach the horizons, but the angels will meet them and strike their faces, so they will turn back. People will turn their backs fleeing, calling out to one another. This is what Allah, exalted is He, refers to: ﴿The Day of Mutual Calling, the Day you will turn back fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [Ghafir 40:32-33]. While they are in that state, suddenly the earth will split open from one side to the other, and they will see a tremendous thing. Such terror will seize them that only Allah knows its extent. Then they will look at the sky, and it will be like molten brass (al-muhl). Then its sun will be darkened, its moon will be eclipsed, its stars will be scattered, and then it will be stripped away from them."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dead know nothing of any of that."

Abu Hurayrah said: "Then who is it that Allah excepted when He said: ﴿And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾ [al-Naml 27:87]?"

He said: "Those are the martyrs. The terror only reaches the living. Those are alive with their Lord, being provided for. Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and will grant them security. And it is the punishment of Allah, which He sends upon the most evil of His creation. This is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [al-Hajj 22:1-2]." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/85).]]

This hadith has been narrated by al-Tabarani, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and others, in a very lengthy form. [[The hadith of the Trumpet was mentioned earlier in the commentary on verse 73 of Surat al-An'am.]]

The purpose of it is that it indicates this convulsion occurs before the Day of the Hour, and it is attributed to the Hour because of its nearness to it, just as one says "the portents of the Hour" and similar expressions. And Allah knows best.

Others said: Rather, that is a terror, a fright, a quaking and a great upheaval that occurs on the Day of Resurrection in the plains of Judgment, after the rising from the graves. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and they argued with several hadiths:

**The first:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Hisham, Qatadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, while on one of his journeys, when the pace of his companions had varied, he raised his voice with these two verses: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾.

When his companions heard that, they hastened their mounts, and they knew that he was at the point of saying something. When they gathered around him, he said: "Do you know what day that is? It is the day when Adam, peace be upon him, will be called, and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will call to him, saying: 'O Adam, send forth your group to the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group of the Fire?' He will say: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine are for the Fire, and one is for Paradise.'"

He said: His companions were struck dumb until they did not show even a smile. When he saw that, he said: "Rejoice and act, for by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creations that never were with anything but that they increased it: Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and whoever perished from the children of Adam and the children of Iblis."

He said: Then their distress was lifted from them. Then he said: "Act and rejoice, for by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are among the people no more than a mole (shamah) on the side of a camel, or a spot on the foreleg of a beast."

Thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the Book of Tafsir from their Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Yahya, that is al-Qattan, from Hisham, that is al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah, with it, similar to this. [[Musnad Ahmad (4/435), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3169), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (11340).]] al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

Another route for this hadith: al-Tirmidhi said: Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, Ibn Judh'an narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: When this was revealed: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ up to His saying: ﴿but the punishment of Allah is severe﴾, it was revealed to him while he was on a journey, and he said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That is the day when Allah will say to Adam: 'Send forth the group of the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group of the Fire?' He will say: 'Nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise.'" Then the Muslims began to weep. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be close to the mark and aim straight, for there has never been a prophethood except that before it there was a period of ignorance (jahiliyyah)." He said: "The number will be taken from the period of ignorance; if it is complete, well and good, otherwise it will be completed from the hypocrites. And your likeness among the nations is only like the spot on the foreleg of a beast, or like the mole on the side of a camel." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." He said: "And I do not know whether he said two-thirds or not."

Similarly, Imam Ahmad narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3168) and Musnad Ahmad (4/432).]] Then al-Tirmidhi also said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

It was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn al-Husayn. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad al-'Adawi, from 'Imran ibn al-Husayn, and he mentioned it.

Likewise, Ibn Jarir narrated from Bundar, from Ghundar, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-'Usrah, and his companions were with him after he had approached Madinah, he recited: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, and he mentioned the hadith. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/86).]] He mentioned something similar to the narration of Ibn Judh'an. And Allah knows best.

**The second hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn al-Tabba' narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Mu'ammari narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: It was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, and he mentioned something similar to the narration of al-Hasan from 'Imran, except that he said: "And whoever perished from the disbelieving jinn and mankind." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/87).]] Ibn Jarir narrated it in full from the hadith of Ma'mar.

**The third hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad, that is Ibn al-'Awwam, narrated to us, Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse and mentioned something similar, and in it he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," so they rejoiced. He also added: "And you are only a part of a thousand parts." [[Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad no. (2235), Kashf al-Astar, with the chain: Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq from Sa'd ibn Sulayman, and he said: "We do not know it to be narrated from Ibn 'Abbas except by this chain." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/69): "I say, part of it is in the Sahih; al-Bazzar narrated it and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Hilal ibn Khabbab, who is trustworthy."]]

**Hadith Four:** Al-Bukhari said, regarding this verse: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Exalted, will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'O Adam!' He will say: 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure.' Then a voice will call out: 'Allah commands you to bring forth from your offspring a group for the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group for the Fire?' He will say: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine [[In T: "and ninety"]].' At that moment every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and the child will turn gray, ﴿And you will see the people as drunk, but they are not drunk; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾. This distressed the people until their faces changed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Out of Gog and Magog, nine hundred and ninety-nine [[In T: "and ninety"]], and out of you, one. Then you are among the people like a black hair on a white ox, or like a white hair on a black ox. I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then he said: 'A third of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then he said: 'Half of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.'"[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4741).]]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, as did Muslim and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir, through several chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3348, 7483); Sahih Muslim, no. (222); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11339).]]

**Hadith Five:** Imam Ahmad said: Ammar [[In T: "Ammara"]] ibn Muhammad, the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ubayda, the meaning being the same, both narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will send forth on the Day of Resurrection a caller [who calls] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]: 'O Adam! Allah commands you to send forth a group from your offspring to the Fire.' Adam will say: 'O Lord, who are they?' It will be said to him: 'Out of every hundred, ninety-nine.'" A man among the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, who then will be saved from among us after this?" He said: "Do you know what you are among the people? You are only like the mark on the chest of a camel."[[Al-Musnad (1/388).]]

Imam Ahmad alone narrated this chain and this text.

**Hadith Six:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghira, who said: Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated to us, that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed you will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." Aisha said: "O Messenger of Allah, will men and women look at one another?" He said: "O Aisha, the matter is too grave for that to concern them." Both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it in the two Sahihs.[[Al-Musnad (6/53); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6527); Sahih Muslim, no. (2855).]]

**Hadith Seven:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Abi Imran, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will a beloved remember his beloved on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "O Aisha, as for three occasions, no: as for at the Scale, until it is heavy or light, no. As for at the flying of the books, when one is given his book in his right hand or in his left hand, no. And when a neck emerges from the Fire, it will encircle them and be enraged at them, and that neck will say: 'I have been assigned to three, I have been assigned to three, I have been assigned to three: I have been assigned to the one who claimed another god along with Allah, and I have been assigned to the one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and I have been assigned to every stubborn tyrant.'" He said: "It will encircle them, and cast them into the depths. And Hell has a bridge finer than a hair and sharper than a sword, upon which are hooks and thorns that seize whomever Allah wills. The people will be upon it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like the swiftest horses and riders. The angels will be saying: 'O Lord, save, save!' So the one who is saved is safe, the one who is scratched is safe, and the one who is thrown headlong into the Fire on his face [[In T: "their faces"]] ..."[[Al-Musnad (6/110).]]

The narrations concerning the terrors of the Day of Resurrection are very numerous, and their proper place is elsewhere. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, meaning: a great matter, a momentous affair, a frightening event, a terrible occurrence, and a wondrous happening.

*Al-zilzal* (convulsion) is what befalls souls of terror and dread, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Day you see it﴾. This is of the type of *damir al-sha'n* (the pronoun referring to the matter or situation itself, without a prior antecedent). For this reason He explained it by saying: ﴿every nursing mother will be distracted from what she was nursing﴾, meaning: she will be preoccupied by the terror of what she sees, distracted from the person most dear to her, and the one who is most compassionate toward him; she will be bewildered about him even while nursing him. For this reason He said ﴿every nursing mother﴾ and did not say "nursing woman" [*murdi'*], and He said ﴿what she was nursing﴾, meaning: her nursling before it was weaned.

* *

His saying: ﴿And every pregnant female will drop her burden﴾, meaning: before its completion, because of the severity of the terror. ﴿And you will see the people as drunk﴾; it is also read as "sakra" (drunk, singular feminine form), meaning: from the severity of the matter they have come to be in, their minds have been bewildered and their intellects absent, so whoever sees them will think they are drunk. ﴿But they are not drunk; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾.

Another route for this hadith: al-Tirmidhi said: Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, Ibn Judh'an narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: When this was revealed: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ up to His saying: ﴿but the punishment of Allah is severe﴾, it was revealed to him while he was on a journey, and he said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That is the day when Allah will say to Adam: 'Send forth the group of the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group of the Fire?' He will say: 'Nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise.'" Then the Muslims began to weep. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be close to the mark and aim straight, for there has never been a prophethood except that before it there was a period of ignorance (jahiliyyah)." He said: "The number will be taken from the period of ignorance; if it is complete, well and good, otherwise it will be completed from the hypocrites. And your likeness among the nations is only like the spot on the foreleg of a beast, or like the mole on the side of a camel." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." So they exclaimed "Allahu akbar." He said: "And I do not know whether he said two-thirds or not."

Similarly, Imam Ahmad narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3168) and Musnad Ahmad (4/432).]] Then al-Tirmidhi also said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

It was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn al-Husayn. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad al-'Adawi, from 'Imran ibn al-Husayn, and he mentioned it.

Likewise, Ibn Jarir narrated from Bundar, from Ghundar, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-'Usrah, and his companions were with him after he had approached Madinah, he recited: ﴿O mankind, be mindful of your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, and he mentioned the hadith. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/86).]] He mentioned something similar to the narration of Ibn Judh'an. And Allah knows best.

**The second hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn al-Tabba' narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Mu'ammari narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: It was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, and he mentioned something similar to the narration of al-Hasan from 'Imran, except that he said: "And whoever perished from the disbelieving jinn and mankind." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/87).]] Ibn Jarir narrated it in full from the hadith of Ma'mar.

**The third hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad, that is Ibn al-'Awwam, narrated to us, Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse and mentioned something similar, and in it he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," so they rejoiced. He also added: "And you are only a part of a thousand parts." [[Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad no. (2235), Kashf al-Astar, with the chain: Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq from Sa'd ibn Sulayman, and he said: "We do not know it to be narrated from Ibn 'Abbas except by this chain." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/69): "I say, part of it is in the Sahih; al-Bazzar narrated it and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Hilal ibn Khabbab, who is trustworthy."]]

**Hadith Four:** Al-Bukhari said, regarding this verse: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Exalted, will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'O Adam!' He will say: 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure.' Then a voice will call out: 'Allah commands you to bring forth from your offspring a group for the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group for the Fire?' He will say: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine [[In T: "and ninety"]].' At that moment every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and the child will turn gray, ﴿And you will see the people as drunk, but they are not drunk; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾. This distressed the people until their faces changed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Out of Gog and Magog, nine hundred and ninety-nine [[In T: "and ninety"]], and out of you, one. Then you are among the people like a black hair on a white ox, or like a white hair on a black ox. I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then he said: 'A third of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then he said: 'Half of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.'"[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4741).]]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, as did Muslim and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir, through several chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3348, 7483); Sahih Muslim, no. (222); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11339).]]

**Hadith Five:** Imam Ahmad said: Ammar [[In T: "Ammara"]] ibn Muhammad, the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ubayda, the meaning being the same, both narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will send forth on the Day of Resurrection a caller [who calls] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]: 'O Adam! Allah commands you to send forth a group from your offspring to the Fire.' Adam will say: 'O Lord, who are they?' It will be said to him: 'Out of every hundred, ninety-nine.'" A man among the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, who then will be saved from among us after this?" He said: "Do you know what you are among the people? You are only like the mark on the chest of a camel."[[Al-Musnad (1/388).]]

Imam Ahmad alone narrated this chain and this text.

**Hadith Six:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghira, who said: Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated to us, that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed you will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." Aisha said: "O Messenger of Allah, will men and women look at one another?" He said: "O Aisha, the matter is too grave for that to concern them." Both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it in the two Sahihs.[[Al-Musnad (6/53); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6527); Sahih Muslim, no. (2855).]]

**Hadith Seven:** Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Abi Imran, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will a beloved remember his beloved on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "O Aisha, as for three occasions, no: as for at the Scale, until it is heavy or light, no. As for at the flying of the books, when one is given his book in his right hand or in his left hand, no. And when a neck emerges from the Fire, it will encircle them and be enraged at them, and that neck will say: 'I have been assigned to three, I have been assigned to three, I have been assigned to three: I have been assigned to the one who claimed another god along with Allah, and I have been assigned to the one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and I have been assigned to every stubborn tyrant.'" He said: "It will encircle them, and cast them into the depths. And Hell has a bridge finer than a hair and sharper than a sword, upon which are hooks and thorns that seize whomever Allah wills. The people will be upon it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like the swiftest horses and riders. The angels will be saying: 'O Lord, save, save!' So the one who is saved is safe, the one who is scratched is safe, and the one who is thrown headlong into the Fire on his face [[In T: "their faces"]] ..."[[Al-Musnad (6/110).]]

The narrations concerning the terrors of the Day of Resurrection are very numerous, and their proper place is elsewhere. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, meaning: a great matter, a momentous affair, a frightening event, a terrible occurrence, and a wondrous happening.

*Al-zilzal* (convulsion) is what befalls souls of terror and dread, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Day you see it﴾. This is of the type of *damir al-sha'n* (the pronoun referring to the matter or situation itself, without a prior antecedent). For this reason He explained it by saying: ﴿every nursing mother will be distracted from what she was nursing﴾, meaning: she will be preoccupied by the terror of what she sees, distracted from the person most dear to her, and the one who is most compassionate toward him; she will be bewildered about him even while nursing him. For this reason He said ﴿every nursing mother﴾ and did not say "nursing woman" [*murdi'*], and He said ﴿what she was nursing﴾, meaning: her nursling before it was weaned.

* *

His saying: ﴿And every pregnant female will drop her burden﴾, meaning: before its completion, because of the severity of the terror. ﴿And you will see the people as drunk﴾; it is also read as "sakra" (drunk, singular feminine form), meaning: from the severity of the matter they have come to be in, their minds have been bewildered and their intellects absent, so whoever sees them will think they are drunk. ﴿But they are not drunk; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾.

God Most High says, censuring those who deny the Resurrection and reject God's power to bring the dead back to life, who turn away from what God sent down to His prophets, and who in their speech, their denial, and their disbelief follow every rebellious devil, from among both men and jinn. This is the condition of the people of misguidance and innovation (bid'ah, newly invented matters in religion), who turn away from the truth and follow falsehood. They abandon the clear truth that God sent down to His Messenger and follow the sayings of the leaders of misguidance, the callers to innovations through their desires and opinions. For this reason He says concerning them and those like them:

﴿And among the people is one who argues about God without knowledge﴾, meaning, without sound knowledge. ﴿And follows every rebellious devil, who has been decreed for him﴾. Mujahid said: this refers to Satan, meaning that it has been written for him by a decree of destiny (kitabah qadariyyah) ﴿that whoever takes him as a friend﴾, meaning follows him and imitates him, ﴿then he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾, meaning he will mislead him in this world and lead him in the Hereafter to the punishment of the Blazing Fire, which is the scorching, painful, distressing, and disturbing fire.

Al-Suddi reported from Abu Malik that this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Ibn Jurayj also said the same.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Salm [in ت and ف: "Ibn Muslim"] al-Basri narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Mahram Abu Qatada narrated to us, al-Ma'mar [in ت: "al-Mu'tamir"] narrated to us, Abu Ka'b al-Makki narrated to us, who said: A wicked man from among the wicked of Quraysh said: "Tell us about your Lord: is He made of gold, or of silver, or of copper?" Then the sky thundered with a loud crash (and qa'qa'ah in the speech of the Arabs means thunder), and the top of his skull fell down before him.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid: A Jew came and said: "O Muhammad, tell us about your Lord: of what is He? Is He of pearl or of ruby?" He said: Then a thunderbolt came and seized him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verses 5–7 (part 1 of 2):

When He (exalted is He) mentioned the one who opposes resurrection and denies the Return (al-ma'ad), He mentioned the proof of His power over the Return from what is witnessed of His initiating creation, saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection﴾, that is, in doubt (shakk) ﴿about the Resurrection﴾, which is the Return (al-ma'ad), the rising of souls and bodies on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed, We created you from dust﴾, that is, the origin of your creation is dust, and this is the dust from which Adam (peace be upon him) was created. ﴿Then from a drop of semen﴾, that is, then He made his offspring from an extract of humble water. ﴿Then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh﴾. This is because when the drop settles in the woman's womb, it remains for forty days in that state, with what gathers to it being added to it. Then it turns into a red clot by Allah's permission, and it remains thus for forty days. Then it transforms and becomes a lump (mudghah), a piece of flesh with no form or outline, and then shaping and outlining begin, so that from it a head and two hands, a chest and belly, two thighs and two legs, and the rest of the limbs are formed. Sometimes the woman miscarries it before shaping and outlining, and sometimes she expels it after it has taken form and outline. Therefore He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾, that is, as you witness it. ﴿That We may make clear to you and settle in the wombs whom We will for an appointed term﴾, that is, and sometimes it remains in the womb; the woman does not expel it nor miscarry it. As Mujahid said regarding His saying (exalted is He): ﴿formed and unformed﴾, he said: it is the miscarriage, formed and unformed. Then when forty days have passed over it while it is a lump, Allah (exalted is He) sends to it an angel who breathes the spirit (al-ruh) into it, and fashions it as Allah (exalted and majestic is He) wills, in beauty or ugliness, male or female, and records its provision, its term, and whether it is wretched or happy. This is as established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is the truthful and the one whose truthfulness is confirmed, told us: "Indeed, the creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty nights, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then he becomes a lump for a similar period. Then Allah sends the angel to him, and he is commanded with four words: to record his deeds, his term, his provision, and whether he is wretched or happy. Then the spirit is breathed into him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6594; Sahih Muslim, no. 2643.]

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, from the hadith of Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: When the drop settles in the womb, an angel takes it in his palm and says: "O Lord, will it be formed or unformed?" If it is said "unformed," it does not become a living soul, and the wombs expel it as blood. If it is said "formed," he says: "O Lord, male or female? Wretched or happy? What is its term? What is its trace? And in what land will it die?" He said: Then it is said to the drop: "Who is your Lord?" It says: "Allah." It is said: "Who is your provider?" It says: "Allah." Then it is said to him: "Go to the Book, for you will find in it the story of this drop." He said: So it is formed, lives for its term, eats its provision, and treads its trace, until its term comes, and it dies and is buried in that place. Then Amir al-Sha'bi recited: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾. When it reaches the lump, it is reversed in the fourth creation, and it becomes a living soul (nasamah). If it is unformed, the wombs expel it as blood, and if it is formed, it is reversed in creation.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The angel enters upon the drop after it settles in the womb by forty or forty-five days, and says: 'O Lord, is it wretched or happy?' Allah says, and the two (angels) write. He says: 'Male or female?' Allah says, and they write. And its deeds, its trace, its provision and its term are written. Then the scrolls are folded up, and nothing is added to what is in them or subtracted from it."

Muslim related it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and from other chains, from Abu al-Tufayl, with a similar meaning. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2644.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Then We bring you out as a child﴾, that is, weak in his body, his hearing, his sight, his senses, his strength, and his intellect. Then Allah gives him strength gradually, and treats him gently, and his parents show him tenderness during the hours of the night and the extremities of the day. Therefore He said: ﴿then that you may reach your maturity (ashudd)﴾, that is, your powers become complete and increase, and he reaches the peak of youth and beauty of appearance.

﴿And among you is he who is taken in death﴾, that is, in the state of his youth and his strength. ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age﴾, which is old age, decrepitude, weakness of strength, intellect and understanding, and the diminishing of conditions from senility (kharaf) and weakness of thought. Therefore He said: ﴿so that he knows after knowledge nothing﴾, as He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent﴾ [al-Rum: 54].

The hafiz Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, Khalid al-Zayyat related to us, Dawud Abu Sulayman related to me, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mar ibn Hazm al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, who raised the hadith (to the Prophet ﷺ), said: "The child until he reaches puberty (al-hinth): whatever good deed he does is written for his father or his mother, and whatever evil deed he does is not written against him or against his parents. When he reaches puberty, Allah sets the pen running over him, and the two angels who are with him are commanded to guard him and to be strict. When he reaches forty years in Islam, Allah protects him from the three afflictions: madness, leprosy, and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, Allah lightens his reckoning. When he reaches sixty, Allah grants him the turning back to Him in a manner He loves. When he reaches seventy, the people of heaven love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah records his good deeds and overlooks his evil deeds. When he reaches ninety, Allah forgives him what came before of his sins and what came after, intercedes for him on behalf of his family, and he is called the captive of Allah on earth. When he reaches the most abject age, ﴿so that he knows after knowledge nothing﴾, Allah writes for him the like of what he used to do of good in his health, and if he does an evil deed, it is not written against him." [Musnad Abi Ya'la, 6/352.]

This is a very strange hadith (hadith gharib jiddan), and it contains severe disapproval (nakarah shadidah). Nevertheless, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal related it in his Musnad, both raised and as a statement of a Companion, and said:

Abu al-Nadr related to us, al-Faraj related to us, Muhammad ibn Amir related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Amiri, from Amr ibn Ja'far, from Anas, who said: "When a Muslim man reaches forty years, Allah protects him from kinds of afflictions: from madness, leprosy and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, Allah makes his reckoning easy. When he reaches sixty, Allah grants him a turning back to Him by which He loves him. When he reaches seventy, Allah loves him, and the people of heaven love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah accepts his good deeds and wipes out his evil deeds. When he reaches ninety, Allah forgives him what came before of his sins and what came after, and he is named the captive of Allah on earth, and he is interceded for on behalf of his family." [Al-Musnad, 2/89.]

Then he said: Hashim related to us, al-Faraj related to us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Amiri related to me, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it. [Al-Musnad, 2/89.]

Imam Ahmad also related it: Anas ibn Iyad related to us, Yusuf ibn Abi Dharrah al-Ansari related to me, from Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one who lives to forty years in Islam, except that Allah turns away from him three kinds of affliction: madness, leprosy, and vitiligo..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith, as before, the same. [Al-Musnad, 3/217; in its chain is Yusuf ibn Abi Dharrah, who is weak.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar also related it from Abdullah ibn Shabib, from Abu Shaybah, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Qatadah al-Udhri, from the son of al-Zuhri's brother, from his paternal uncle, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No servant who lives to forty years in Islam, except that Allah turns away from him kinds of affliction: madness, leprosy, and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty years, Allah makes his reckoning easy. When he reaches sixty years, Allah grants him the turning back to Him by which He loves. When he reaches seventy, Allah forgives him what came before of his sins and what came after, he is named the captive of Allah, and the people of heaven love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah accepts from him his good deeds and overlooks his evil deeds. When he reaches ninety, Allah forgives him what came before of his sin and what came after, and he is named the captive of Allah on His earth, and he is interceded for on behalf of the people of his household." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3588, Kashf al-Astar.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless﴾: this is another proof of His power to revive the dead, just as He revives the dead earth, which is the barren land (al-qahlah) in which there is no plant or anything.

Qatadah said: "Dusty and crumbled." Al-Suddi said: "Dead."

﴿So when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind﴾, that is: when Allah sends down rain upon it, ﴿it stirs﴾, that is, it moves and comes to life after its death, ﴿and swells﴾, that is, it rises, when the soil within it has settled. Then it causes to grow what is in it of colors and kinds, of fruits and crops, and various plants, differing in their colors, tastes, smells, shapes, and benefits. Therefore He (exalted is He) said: ﴿and grows every lovely kind﴾, that is, of beautiful appearance and pleasant scent.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾, that is, the Creator, the Ordainer, the Doer of what He wills, ﴿and because He gives life to the dead﴾ [that is, as He revived the dead earth and caused these kinds to grow from it; ﴿Indeed, He who revived it is certainly the Giver of life to the dead﴾] [addition from manuscripts F and A], ﴿and He is over all things competent﴾ [Fussilat: 39]. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82].

And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it (﴿وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا﴾), meaning: it will certainly occur, with no doubt or uncertainty about it, and that Allah will raise those who are in the graves (﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ﴾), meaning: He will restore them after they have become dust in their graves, and bring them into existence after non-existence, as He says: ﴿And he sets forth for Us a similitude and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knower of every creation. He who made for you from the green tree fire, and thereupon you ignite [from it]."﴾ [Yasin: 78-80]. The verses on this subject are many.

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Ya'la informed us, from 'Ata', from WakI' ibn Hudus, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, whose name is Laqit ibn 'Amir, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, will all of us see our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection? And what is the sign of that in His creation?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not all of you see the moon, alone?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Then Allah is greater." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead, and what is the sign of that in His creation?" He said: "Did you not pass by the valley of your people, barren, [then] you passed by it again, verdant and stirring?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Thus Allah gives life to the dead, and that is His sign in His creation."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it, through the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Ya'la informed us, from 'Ata', from WakI' ibn Hudus, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, whose name is Laqit ibn 'Amir, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, will all of us see our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection? And what is the sign of that in His creation?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not all of you see the moon, alone?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Then Allah is greater." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead, and what is the sign of that in His creation?" He said: "Did you not pass by the valley of your people, barren, [then] you passed by it again, verdant and stirring?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Thus Allah gives life to the dead, and that is His sign in His creation."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it, through the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Then Imam Ahmad also narrated it: 'Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir informed us, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Abu Razin al-'Uqayli, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead?' He said: 'Did you pass by a land of yours that was barren, then you passed by it fertile?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Thus is the resurrection.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ubays ibn Marhum narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Abi al-Sumayt narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Hajjaj, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "Whoever knows that Allah is the Manifest Truth, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah raises those in the graves, enters Paradise." Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verse 8–10:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the state of the astray, ignorant imitators in His words, ﴿And among mankind is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾, He mentioned in this verse the state of the leaders of disbelief and innovation who call to misguidance. He said: ﴿And among mankind is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾, meaning: without sound reason and without clear, sound transmission, but merely by opinion and whim.

* *

His words ﴿turning aside [thāniya ʿiṭfih]﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: arrogant toward the truth when it is called to. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, said: ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfih﴾ means twisting his neck, which is his neck, meaning: he turns away from the truth to which he is called, with his neck, out of arrogance. Like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And in Moses [too there was a sign], when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority. But he turned away with his supporters and said, "A magician or a madman."﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 38, 39]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion﴾ [An-Nisa: 61]. And He said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads and you see them turning away while they are arrogant﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 5]. And Luqman said to his son: ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾ [Luqman: 18], meaning: do not incline it away from them out of arrogance toward them. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as though he did not hear them, as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [Luqman: 7].

* *

His words ﴿to mislead from the way of Allah﴾: Some of them said: this is the lam of consequence, because he may not intend that. It may also be the lam of causation. Then either the intended meaning is the obstinate ones, or the intended meaning is that this doer of this act is one whom We have created with this disposition which makes him among those who lead astray from the way of Allah.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿For him in this world is disgrace﴾, which is humiliation and abasement, just as when he was arrogant toward the signs of Allah, Allah inflicted upon him humiliation in this world, and punished him therein before the Hereafter, because worldly matters are his greatest concern and the extent of his knowledge. ﴿And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning. [It will be said], "This is for what your hands have put forward."﴾

Meaning: it is said to him this as reproach and rebuke. ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, like His words, exalted is He: ﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire. Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. Taste it; indeed, you were the mighty, the noble. Indeed, this is what you used to doubt﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 47–50].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hisham informed us, from al-Hasan who said: It reached me that one of them is burned seventy thousand times a day.

When He mentioned the people of misguidance, the wretched, He followed with mention of the righteous, the blessed, from among those who believed with their hearts, and confirmed their faith by their deeds, so they did righteous actions of every kind of act of worship, [and abstained from the forbidden things] [[addition from manuscripts F and A.]] Therefore this brought them to dwell in the lofty ranks, in the gardens of the Paradises.

And when He mentioned that He misguides those and guides these, He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills﴾

Ibn Abbas said: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muhammad (ﷺ) in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿let him stretch out a rope﴾, meaning a cord, ﴿to the sky﴾, meaning the sky of his house, ﴿then let him cut it off﴾. He says: then let him hang himself with it. Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Abu al-Jawza, Qatadah, and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿let him stretch out [[In T: "And let him stretch out."]] a rope to the sky﴾, meaning, let him reach the sky, for help comes to Muhammad from the sky, ﴿then let him cut off﴾ that help from him, if he is able to do so.

The saying of Ibn Abbas and his companions is more correct and clearer in meaning, and more forceful in mockery. The meaning is: whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muhammad, his Book and his religion, let him go and kill himself, if that is what enrages him, for Allah will certainly help him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand. The Day when the wrongdoers' excuse will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51, 52]. Therefore He said: ﴿then let him look: does his plotting remove that which enrages him?﴾

Al-Suddi said: meaning: concerning the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ata al-Khurasani said: ﴿then let him look: does that heal what he feels in his chest of rage?﴾

And His saying: ﴿Thus We have sent it down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿as clear signs﴾, meaning manifest in both its wording and its meaning, a proof from Allah to the people. ﴿And that Allah guides whom He wills﴾, meaning He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and to Him belongs perfect wisdom and the decisive proof in this matter. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 23]. As for Him, it is by His wisdom, His mercy, His justice, His knowledge, His dominion and His majesty; there is no one to repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.

Ibn Abbas said: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muhammad (ﷺ) in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿let him stretch out a rope﴾, meaning a cord, ﴿to the sky﴾, meaning the sky of his house, ﴿then let him cut it off﴾. He says: then let him hang himself with it. Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Abu al-Jawza, Qatadah, and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿let him stretch out [[In T: "And let him stretch out."]] a rope to the sky﴾, meaning, let him reach the sky, for help comes to Muhammad from the sky, ﴿then let him cut off﴾ that help from him, if he is able to do so.

The saying of Ibn Abbas and his companions is more correct and clearer in meaning, and more forceful in mockery. The meaning is: whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muhammad, his Book and his religion, let him go and kill himself, if that is what enrages him, for Allah will certainly help him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand. The Day when the wrongdoers' excuse will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51, 52]. Therefore He said: ﴿then let him look: does his plotting remove that which enrages him?﴾

Al-Suddi said: meaning: concerning the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ata al-Khurasani said: ﴿then let him look: does that heal what he feels in his chest of rage?﴾

And His saying: ﴿Thus We have sent it down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿as clear signs﴾, meaning manifest in both its wording and its meaning, a proof from Allah to the people. ﴿And that Allah guides whom He wills﴾, meaning He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and to Him belongs perfect wisdom and the decisive proof in this matter. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 23]. As for Him, it is by His wisdom, His mercy, His justice, His knowledge, His dominion and His majesty; there is no one to repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the people of these different religions among the believers, and others besides them: the Jews, the Sabians (and the details about them, and the differences of people concerning them, have already been presented in Surah al-Baqarah), the Christians, the Magians, and those who associated partners, worshipping others alongside Allah. Indeed, He ﴿will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, and He judges between them with justice [[In the manuscript T: "with punishment."]], so He admits into Paradise whoever believed in Him, and admits into the Fire whoever disbelieved in Him [[In manuscripts T and A: "to."]]. Indeed, He is Witness over their deeds, Guardian over their words, and Knowing of their inner secrets and what their hearts conceal.

Ibn Kathir said: He, Exalted is He, informs that He alone is the One deserving of worship, with no partner. Everything prostrates to His majesty, willingly or unwillingly, and each thing's prostration is specific to it, as He said: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, how their shadows turn to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled?﴾ [An-Nahl: 48]. Here He said: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth﴾, meaning: the angels in the regions of the heavens, and the animals in all directions, among mankind, the jinn, the beasts and the birds, ﴿and there is not a thing but that it glorifies Him with His praise﴾ [Al-Isra: 44].

As for His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon and the stars﴾, He mentioned these specifically because they have been worshipped besides Allah, so He made clear that they prostrate to their Creator, and that they are subordinate and subjected. ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him that you worship﴾ [Fussilat: 37].

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know where this sun goes?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then it is asked permission, and it is nearly said to it: 'Return from where you came.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4803) and Sahih Muslim no. (159)].

In the Musnad and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, in the hadith about the eclipse: "The sun and the moon are two signs among the creation of Allah, and they do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for his life, but when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, manifests Himself to something of His creation, it humbles itself before Him."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: There is no star, nor sun, nor moon in the sky but that it falls prostrate to Allah when it sets, then it does not turn away until it is given permission, so it takes its course to the right until it returns to its rising point.

As for the mountains and trees, their prostration is by the shade of their shadows turning to the right and to the left. From Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw myself last night while I was asleep, as if I were praying behind a tree. I prostrated, and the tree prostrated at my prostration. I heard it saying: 'O Allah, record for me with You a reward through it, remove from me through it a burden, make it for me with You a treasure, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dawud.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) then recited a prostration verse and prostrated, and I heard him saying the same as the man had reported the tree saying.

Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (579) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1053). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, which we only know through this route."].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the animals﴾, meaning all living creatures.

It has also come in a hadith related by Imam Ahmad that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade taking the backs of animals as pulpits [Abu Dawud also narrated it in his Sunan no. (2567) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]: "For a mount may be better and more mindful of Allah than its rider."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and many of mankind﴾, meaning: prostrates to Allah willingly, choosing it, worshipping Him thereby. ﴿and many deserve the punishment﴾, meaning: of those who refuse, turn away and are arrogant. ﴿And whomever Allah humiliates, there is no honourer for him. Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Shaiban al-Ramli told us, al-Haddah told us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali who said: It was said to 'Ali: "Indeed, there is a man here who speaks about the Will." So 'Ali said to him: "O servant of Allah, did Allah create you as He wills or as you will?" He said: "Rather, as He wills." He said: "Then does He make you ill when He wills or when you will?" He said: "Rather, when He wills." He said: "Then does He cure you when He wills or when you will?" He said: "Rather, when He wills." He said: "Then does He admit you wherever you wish or wherever He wills?" He said: "Rather, wherever He wills." He said: "By Allah, if you had said otherwise, I would have struck the one in whom your eyes are with the sword."

From Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam recites the prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping, saying: 'Woe is me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so for him is Paradise; and I was commanded to prostrate and I refused, so for me is the Fire.'" Narrated by Muslim [Sahih Muslim no. (81)].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' told us, both said: Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Mashraḥ ibn Ha'an Abu Mus'ab al-Ma'afiri told us, he said: I heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir say: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, has Surah al-Hajj been preferred over the rest of the Qur'an by two prostrations?" He said: "Yes, so whoever does not prostrate in them, let him not recite them."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah, with the same chain [Musnad (4/151), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1402) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (578)]. al-Tirmidhi said: "It is not strong [laysa bi-qawiy]." But this is open to question, for Ibn Lahi'ah has explicitly stated hearing in it, and the most that they criticised him for is tadlis (concealment).

Abu Dawud said in al-Marasil: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Sarh told us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from 'Amir ibn Jashib, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surah al-Hajj has been preferred over the Qur'an by two prostrations."

Then Abu Dawud said: "It has been traced back through a route other than this, but it is not sound [wa la yasihh]."

al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili said: Ibn Abi Dawud told us, Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah told us, al-Walid told us, Abu 'Amr told us, Hafs ibn 'Anan told us, Nafi' told me, Abu al-Jahm told me: that 'Umar performed two prostrations in al-Hajj while he was at al-Jabiyah, and said: "Indeed, this has been preferred by two prostrations" [al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (2/317) through Nafi' from a man of Egypt who prayed with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned the like].

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Harith ibn Sa'id al-'Utaqi, from 'Abdullah ibn Munin, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught him fifteen prostrations in the Qur'an, three of them in al-Mufassal, and two in Surah al-Hajj [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1401) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1057)]. These are witnesses which strengthen one another.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 22, verses 19–22:

It is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn 'Ubad, from Abu Dharr, that he used to swear an oath that this verse: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ was revealed concerning Hamzah and his two companions, and 'Utbah and his two companions, on the day they came forth at Badr.

The wording of al-Bukhari when interpreting it, then al-Bukhari said:

Al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father, Abu Mijlaz narrated to us from Qays ibn 'Ubad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "I will be the first to fall to his knees before the Most Merciful for the dispute on the Day of Resurrection." Qays said: "And concerning them this verse was revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾." He said: "They are those who came forth at Badr: 'Ali, Hamzah, and 'Ubaydah, and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah said, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "The Muslims and the People of the Book disputed. The People of the Book said: 'Our Prophet came before your Prophet, and our Book came before your book, so we are more deserving of God than you.' The Muslims said: 'Our Book overrides all the books, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, so we are more deserving of God than you.' So God granted Islam victory over those who opposed it, and revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾." Similarly al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

Shu'bah said, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "A believer and a disbeliever."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding this verse: "It is the likeness of the disbeliever and the believer who dispute concerning the Resurrection." He also said, in another narration, that he and 'Ata' said regarding this verse: "They are the believers and the disbelievers."

'Ikrimah said: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are Paradise and Hellfire. Hellfire said: 'Make me for punishment,' and Paradise said: 'Make me for mercy.'"

The view of Mujahid and 'Ata' that the intended meaning here is the disbelievers and the believers encompasses all the statements, and includes the incident of the day of Badr and other events, for the believers seek to support the religion of God, while the disbelievers seek to extinguish the light of faith, forsake the truth, and make falsehood prevail. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it is good. Therefore He said: ﴿So those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, meaning: garments of fire will be fashioned and cut for them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "[They are] of copper, which is the most intensely hot of things when heated."

﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads. By it, that which is in their bellies and the skins will be melted﴾, meaning: when boiling water, which is hot water at extreme heat, is poured over their heads.

Sa'id [ibn Jubayr] [added from F and A] said: "It is molten copper, which melts what is in their bellies of fat and intestines." This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others. Likewise their skins melt; Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id said: "They fall off."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ibrahim Abu Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed the boiling water is poured over their heads, and it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts what is in their insides until it reaches their feet, and that is the ṣihr (melting), then they are restored as they were."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, and said: "Hasan sahih." Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu Nu'aym, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, I heard 'Abd Allah ibn al-Surri say: "An angel comes to him carrying the vessel with tongs because of its heat. When he brings it near his face, he recoils from it. He said: Then he raises a club with him and strikes his head with it, so his brain is spilled, then he pours the vessel from his brain, so it reaches his insides from his brain. That is His saying: ﴿By it, that which is in their bellies and the skins will be melted﴾."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And for them are maqami' of iron﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who said: "If a club of iron were placed on the earth, and both jinn and humans gathered to lift it, they would not be able to lift it from the earth."

And Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If the mountain were struck with an iron club, it would shatter, then return as it was. And if a bucket of ghassaq were poured out in this world, the people of this world would be stunk out."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: ﴿And for them are maqami' of iron﴾: "They are struck with them, so each limb falls in its place, and they call out for destruction (thubur)."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾: al-A'mash narrated from Abu Zabyan, from Salman, who said: "The Fire is black and dark; its flame does not give light, nor its ember." Then he recited: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾.

Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding this verse: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾: "It has reached me that the people of the Fire, in the Fire, do not breathe."

Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad said: "By God, they do not hope to get out. Indeed their feet are shackled, and their hands are bound, but its flames lift them up, and its clubs drive them back."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾, like His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [As-Sajdah: 20]. The meaning of the speech is that they are humiliated with punishment, in word and in deed.

Sa'id [ibn Jubayr] [added from F and A] said: "It is molten copper, which melts what is in their bellies of fat and intestines." This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others. Likewise their skins melt; Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id said: "They fall off."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ibrahim Abu Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed the boiling water is poured over their heads, and it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts what is in their insides until it reaches their feet, and that is the ṣihr (melting), then they are restored as they were."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, and said: "Hasan sahih." Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu Nu'aym, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, I heard 'Abd Allah ibn al-Surri say: "An angel comes to him carrying the vessel with tongs because of its heat. When he brings it near his face, he recoils from it. He said: Then he raises a club with him and strikes his head with it, so his brain is spilled, then he pours the vessel from his brain, so it reaches his insides from his brain. That is His saying: ﴿By it, that which is in their bellies and the skins will be melted﴾."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And for them are maqami' of iron﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who said: "If a club of iron were placed on the earth, and both jinn and humans gathered to lift it, they would not be able to lift it from the earth."

And Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If the mountain were struck with an iron club, it would shatter, then return as it was. And if a bucket of ghassaq were poured out in this world, the people of this world would be stunk out."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: ﴿And for them are maqami' of iron﴾: "They are struck with them, so each limb falls in its place, and they call out for destruction (thubur)."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾: al-A'mash narrated from Abu Zabyan, from Salman, who said: "The Fire is black and dark; its flame does not give light, nor its ember." Then he recited: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾.

Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding this verse: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress, they will be returned into it﴾: "It has reached me that the people of the Fire, in the Fire, do not breathe."

Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad said: "By God, they do not hope to get out. Indeed their feet are shackled, and their hands are bound, but its flames lift them up, and its clubs drive them back."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾, like His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [As-Sajdah: 20]. The meaning of the speech is that they are humiliated with punishment, in word and in deed.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 22, verses 19–22:

It is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn 'Ubad, from Abu Dharr, that he used to swear an oath that this verse: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ was revealed concerning Hamzah and his two companions, and 'Utbah and his two companions, on the day they came forth at Badr.

The wording of al-Bukhari when interpreting it, then al-Bukhari said:

Al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father, Abu Mijlaz narrated to us from Qays ibn 'Ubad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "I will be the first to fall to his knees before the Most Merciful for the dispute on the Day of Resurrection." Qays said: "And concerning them this verse was revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾." He said: "They are those who came forth at Badr: 'Ali, Hamzah, and 'Ubaydah, and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah said, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "The Muslims and the People of the Book disputed. The People of the Book said: 'Our Prophet came before your Prophet, and our Book came before your book, so we are more deserving of God than you.' The Muslims said: 'Our Book overrides all the books, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, so we are more deserving of God than you.' So God granted Islam victory over those who opposed it, and revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾." Similarly al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

Shu'bah said, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "A believer and a disbeliever."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding this verse: "It is the likeness of the disbeliever and the believer who dispute concerning the Resurrection." He also said, in another narration, that he and 'Ata' said regarding this verse: "They are the believers and the disbelievers."

'Ikrimah said: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are Paradise and Hellfire. Hellfire said: 'Make me for punishment,' and Paradise said: 'Make me for mercy.'"

The view of Mujahid and 'Ata' that the intended meaning here is the disbelievers and the believers encompasses all the statements, and includes the incident of the day of Badr and other events, for the believers seek to support the religion of God, while the disbelievers seek to extinguish the light of faith, forsake the truth, and make falsehood prevail. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it is good. Therefore He said: ﴿So those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, meaning: garments of fire will be fashioned and cut for them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verse 23–24:

When Allah, the Exalted, informed us about the state of the people of the Fire, seeking refuge with Allah from their condition and from the punishment, torment, burning and shackles they endure, and from the garments of fire prepared for them, He mentioned the state of the people of Paradise—we ask Allah, by His grace and generosity, to admit us into Paradise—and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. That is, they flow through its sides, its surroundings and its edges, and beneath its trees and its palaces, and they direct them wherever and however they wish. ﴿They will be adorned therein﴾ with ornaments (ḥilyah), ﴿they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾, that is, on their hands, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh): "The ornament will reach the believer wherever the ablution (wuḍū') reaches." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (246), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "In Paradise there is an angel whom, if I wished to name, I would name. He fashions ornaments for the people of Paradise from the moment Allah created him until the Day of Resurrection. If a single bracelet of his were displayed, it would outshine the rays of the sun, just as the sun outshines the light of the moon."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾: in contrast to the garments of the people of the Fire, which were cut out for them, the clothing of these people is silk, both its brocade (istabraq) and its fine silk (sundus), as He said: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink. Indeed, this is for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insan: 21, 22]. In the Sahih it is narrated: "Do not wear silk or brocade in this world, for whoever wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter." [The hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5426), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2067), from the hadith of Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him).]

'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: "Whoever does not wear silk in the Hereafter will not enter Paradise." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they are guided to the good speech﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ [Ibrahim: 23], and His saying: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. How excellent is the final home."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23, 24], and His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech or sinful speech, except the saying, "Peace, peace."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 25, 26]. So they are guided to the place where they hear good speech, ﴿and they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾ [al-Furqan: 75]. This is unlike the people of the Fire, who are humiliated by the speech with which they are rebuked and reproached, and it is said to them: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾, that is, to the place where they praise their Lord for what He has bestowed upon them, favored them with and granted them, as came in the Sahih: "They will be inspired to glorify (tasbih) and praise (tahmid) Allah just as they are inspired to breathe."

Some of the exegetes said regarding His saying: ﴿And they are guided to the good speech﴾ that it means the Qur'an. It was also said: "There is no god but Allah." And it was said: the prescribed remembrances (al-adhkar al-mashru'ah). ﴿And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾, that is, the straight path in this world. All of this does not contradict what we have mentioned, and Allah knows best.
