He (Exalted is He) says, rebuking the disbelievers for barring the believers from coming to the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), from performing their rites there, and for claiming that they are its guardians: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are none but the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 34].

In this verse there is evidence [of] [[added from T.]] that it is Medinan, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is grave, but barring from the way of God, disbelief in Him, barring from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it are graver in the sight of God﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 217]. And He said here: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God and the Sacred Mosque﴾, meaning: among their characteristics, along with their disbelief, is that they bar from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque, that is, they bar from the Sacred Mosque whoever among the believers wishes to visit it, though they are in reality the most entitled of people to it. This construction in this verse is like His saying: ﴿Those who believe and whose hearts are at rest in the remembrance of God. Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 28], meaning: among their characteristics is that their hearts find rest in the remembrance of God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿[The Mosque] which We made for mankind, equal for the resident therein and the visitor﴾ [meaning: they prevent people from reaching the Sacred Mosque, though God has made it, by law, equal, with no distinction between the one who dwells in it and the one who is far from it, distant in residence. ﴿Equal for the resident therein and the visitor﴾] [[added from F.]]. Among this is the equality of people in the dwellings (ribaa') of Makkah and its residence, as 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿equal for the resident therein and the visitor﴾: he said, "The people of Makkah and others alight in the Sacred Mosque."

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿equal for the resident therein and the visitor﴾: "The people of Makkah and others are equal in it regarding dwellings." Abu Salih, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd [ibn Aslam] [[added from A.]] said likewise.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "Its inhabitants and non-inhabitants are equal in it."

This question was disputed between al-Shafi'i and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh at Masjid al-Khayf, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal was also present. Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him [[in F: "may God be pleased with him"; in A: "may God Most High be pleased with him."]], held that the dwellings of Makkah may be owned, inherited, and rented out. He argued with the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of God, will you alight tomorrow in your house [[in F: "in your house"]] in Makkah?' He said: 'Did 'Aqil leave us any dwellings?'" Then he said: "The disbeliever does not inherit from the Muslim, nor the Muslim from the disbeliever." This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6764) and Sahih Muslim no. (1614) from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd, may God be pleased with him.]]. [And by what is established: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab bought a house in Makkah from Safwan ibn Umayyah, and made it a prison for four thousand dirhams.] And Tawus and 'Amr ibn Dinar said likewise.

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, however, held that they may be inherited but not rented out. This is the position of a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and Mujahid and 'Ata' explicitly affirmed it. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh argued with what Ibn Majah related from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from 'Isa ibn Yunus, from 'Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Husayn [[in T: "Jubayr"; in F, A: "Haywah".]], from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Alqamah ibn Nadlah, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ died, and Abu Bakr and 'Umar [were alive], and the dwellings of Makkah were called only 'al-sawaib' (free to all): whoever needed, lived in them, and whoever was well off, let others live in them."[[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3107), and it is mursal (a hadith whose chain omits a companion).]]

'Abd al-Razzaq [said], from Ibn Mujahid, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, that he said: "The selling of the houses of Makkah and their renting is not lawful."

He also said, from Ibn Jurayj: "'Ata' used to forbid renting in the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and he informed me that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to forbid the closing of the houses of Makkah with doors, so that the pilgrim could alight in their courtyards. The first to close his house was Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab sent to him about it. He said: 'Give me time, O Commander of the Believers, for I was a merchant, and I wanted to make two doors to shield my back.' He said: 'Then that is acceptable.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Mansur, from Mujahid, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "O people of Makkah, do not make doors for your houses, so that the desert-dweller may alight wherever he wishes."

He said: "Ma'mar informed us, from one who heard 'Ata' say [concerning His saying] [[added from F, A.]]: ﴿equal for the resident therein and the visitor﴾: 'They alight wherever they wish.'"

Al-Daraqutni related from the hadith of Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, as a statement attributed to him (mawquf) [[in F, A: "as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet)".]]: "Whoever consumes the rent of the houses of Makkah consumes fire."[[Sunan al-Daraqutni (2/300).]]

"And Imam Ahmad took a middle position [as transmitted by his son Salih], saying: they may be owned and inherited, but not rented out, combining the evidences. And God knows best."

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾: some of the grammarians among the exegetes said: the letter ba' (بِ) here is extra (za'idah), like His saying: ﴿grows oil [tunbitu bi-al-duhn]﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 20], meaning: "grows the oil (tunbitu al-duhn)." Likewise His saying: ﴿whoever intends therein with deviation [bi-ilhad]﴾ has the sense of "deviation (ilhadan)." And as al-A'sha said:

"Our spears guaranteed the provision of our dependants, between the cooking pots and the bare-headed (al-sarih al-ajrad)."

And another said:

"In a Yemeni valley, whose ground grows the thorny shrub (al-shabb), and beneath it, the markh and al-shababan..."

But the better view is that the verb here is taken to include the meaning of "to resolve" (yahumm), and for this reason it is followed by the ba' (بِ), so He says: ﴿whoever intends therein with deviation with injustice﴾, meaning: he resolves in it upon a grave matter of major sins.

* *

His saying: ﴿with injustice﴾ means: deliberately and intentionally, [meaning] that it is injustice, not one that is done under interpretation, as Ibn Jurayj related from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is [the deliberate intent] [[added from F, A.]]."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿with injustice﴾ means with shirk (associating partners with God)."

Mujahid said: "That other than God be worshipped in it." Qatadah and others said likewise.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿with injustice﴾ is that you make lawful within the Sanctuary what God has forbidden you, of speech or killing, so that you wrong one who does not wrong you, and kill one who does not kill you. When he does that, the painful punishment is due to him."

Mujahid said: "﴿with injustice﴾: he does an evil deed in it."

This is a particular feature of the Sanctuary: the one who resolves upon evil in it is punished, if he is determined upon it, even if he does not carry it out. As Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir:

Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Shu'bah informed us, from al-Suddi, that he heard Murrah relate from 'Abd Allah [i.e., Ibn Mas'ud] concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾: he said: "If a man intended in it deviation with injustice, while he was at 'Adan Abyan, God would have caused him to taste of the painful punishment."

Shu'bah said: "He raised it to us (i.e., attributed it to the Prophet), but I do not raise it for you." Yazid said: "He has raised it." And Ahmad related it from Yazid ibn Harun, with this [chain].[[Musnad Ahmad (1/428).]]

[I say: this chain] [[added from F, A.]] is sahih according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, but its being mawquf (a statement of a companion) is more likely than its being marfu' (attributed to the Prophet). For this reason Shu'bah insisted on its being mawquf, as a statement of Ibn Mas'ud. Likewise, Asbat and Sufyan al-Thawri related it from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud as mawquf. And God knows best.

Al-Thawri said, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "No man resolves upon an evil deed and it is written against him; and if a man at 'Adan Abyan had resolved to kill a man in this House, God would have caused him to taste the painful punishment." Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said likewise.

Sufyan [al-Thawri] [[added from F.]] said, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning "deviation in it": "No, by God, and yes, by God." It is also related from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, the like.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Reviling a servant is injustice, and what is above it."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata', from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾: he said: "The trade of the ruler in it."

And from Ibn 'Umar: "Selling food in Makkah [[added from T, F, A.]] is deviation."

Habib ibn Abi Thabit [in T: "Jundab"] said: "﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾: he said: the hoarder in Makkah." And others said likewise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-Jawhari related to us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from his paternal uncle 'Umarah ibn Thawban: Musa ibn Badhan related to me, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Hoarding food in Makkah is deviation."[[Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan no. (2020), and al-Fakihi in Tarikh Makkah no. (1771), by way of Abu 'Asim with this chain.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr [in T, F: "Bukr"] related to us: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us: 'Ata' ibn Dinar related to me: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning God's saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾: "It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent him with two men, one of them a Muhajir and the other an Ansari. They boasted about lineages, and 'Abd Allah ibn Unays became angry, and killed the Ansari. Then he apostatized from Islam and fled to Makkah, and this verse was revealed about him: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice﴾, meaning: whoever takes refuge in the Sanctuary with deviation, that is, with turning away from Islam."

And although these reports indicate that these things are of deviation, deviation is more general than that. Rather, in them is an alert to what is graver than them. For this reason, when the people of the Elephant intended to destroy the House, God sent against them birds in flocks, ﴿pelting them with stones of baked clay, and He made them like eaten stalks﴾ [Al-Fil: 4-5], meaning: He destroyed them and made them an example and a warning for everyone who intends it evil. And for this reason it is established in the hadith that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "An army will invade this House, until when they are in a desert of the earth, the first of them and the last of them will be swallowed up by the earth..." — the hadith.[[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2118), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Kunasah related to us: Ishaq ibn Sa'id related to us, from his father, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar came to 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr and said: "O son of al-Zubayr, beware of deviation in the sanctuary of God, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Indeed, a man of Quraysh will deviate in it, and if his sins were weighed against the sins of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), they would outweigh them.' So take care, lest you be him."[[Musnad Ahmad (2/136).]]

He also said, [in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As] [[added from F, A.]]: Hashim related to us: Ishaq ibn Sa'id related to us: Sa'id ibn 'Amr related to us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr came to Ibn al-Zubayr while he was sitting in al-Hijr, and said: "O son of al-Zubayr, beware of deviation in the Sanctuary, for I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'He will make it lawful, and a man of Quraysh will make it lawful for himself, and if his sins were weighed against the sins of the two weighty ones, they would outweigh them.'" He said: "So take care, lest you be [[in T: 'lest he be'; in F: 'lest you be']] him."[[Musnad Ahmad (12/912) (no. 21912 in the edition).]]

None of the authors of the books [of hadith] has recorded it from these two routes.

This passage contains a rebuke and reproach to those among the Quraysh who worshipped other than God and associated partners with Him, in the very place that was founded from the first day on the Oneness of God and worshipping Him alone, with no partner. He, exalted is He, mentions that He settled Abraham in the place of the House, that is, He guided him to it, handed it over to him, and permitted him to build it.

Many have used this as evidence for the view that "Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to build the Ancient House, and that it was not built before him," as is established in the Sahih [in manuscript F: "al-Sahihain"] from Abu Dharr, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, which mosque was placed first?" He said: "The Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)." I said: "How long was between them?" He said: "Forty years." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3366, and Sahih Muslim, no. 520]

God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96–97, to the end of the verse]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We charged Abraham and Ishmael: Purify My House for those who circumambulate, those who stay in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125].

We have already mentioned what has come concerning the building of the House from the authentic reports and narrations, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary [see the commentary on verse 125 of Surah al-Baqarah].

God, exalted is He, said here: ﴿that you not associate anything with Me﴾, meaning: [do not associate] His son with My name alone. ﴿And purify My House﴾: Mujahid and Qatadah said: from shirk (associating partners with God). ﴿For those who circumambulate and those who stand and those who bow and prostrate﴾, meaning: make it sincerely for those who worship God alone, with no partner.

The one who circumambulates it (tawaf, circumambulation) is well known, and it is the most specific of acts of worship at the House, for it is not performed at any other place on earth. ﴿And those who stand﴾ means in prayer (salah); therefore He said: ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾. Thus He combined circumambulation with prayer, because both are only legislated in connection with the House: circumambulation is around it, and prayer is directed toward it in most circumstances, except what is excepted from prayer facing it, such as when the direction of the qiblah is uncertain, during warfare, and voluntary (nafilah) prayer while traveling. And God knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage (hajj)﴾ means: call out to the people, inviting them to the pilgrimage to this House which We commanded you to build. It is mentioned that he said: "O Lord, how can I convey this to the people when my voice cannot reach them?" It was said: "Call out, and upon Us is the conveying."

So he stood upon his station (maqam). It is said he stood upon the Stone, and it is said upon al-Safa, and it is said upon Abu Qubays. And he said: "O people, indeed your Lord has taken a House, so make pilgrimage to it." It is said that the mountains lowered themselves until the voice reached the ends of the earth, and it made heard whoever was in the wombs and the loins, and everything that heard him answered him, from stone, clay and tree, and whoever God had written would make pilgrimage until the Day of Resurrection said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk (Here I am, O God, here I am)."

This is the substance of what has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and many others of the early generations (salaf). And God knows best.

It was recorded by Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari], and Ibn Abi Hatim at length [in manuscript F: "in full"]. [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/106).]

* *

His saying: ﴿They will come to you on foot, and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep mountain pass﴾: some scholars who hold that performing hajj on foot is superior to performing it riding, for one who is able to do so, have used this verse as evidence, because He mentioned them first, which indicates concern for them and the strength of their resolve and the intensity of their determination. The view held by most scholars, however, is that performing hajj riding is superior, following the example of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for he performed hajj riding despite his full strength, peace be upon him.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will come from every deep mountain pass﴾ means: from every path, as He said: ﴿And We made in it wide roads as ways﴾ [al-Anbiya': 31].

* *

His saying: ﴿deep﴾ means: distant. This was said by Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Suddi, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Thawri, and others.

This verse is like His saying, exalted is He, reporting about Abraham, when he said in his supplication: ﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them﴾ [Ibrahim: 37]. No one among the people of Islam is without longing to see the Ka'bah and to circumambulate it, so people head toward it from all directions and regions.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿that they may witness benefits for them﴾: "The benefits of this world and the Hereafter. As for the benefits of the Hereafter, they are the pleasure of Allah; and as for the benefits of this world, they are what they obtain of the benefits of the animals [[In T, F, A: "slaughtering" (al-dhaba'ih)]] , profit and trade." Likewise Mujahid and others said: "It refers to the benefits of this world and the Hereafter," like His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you seek bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 198].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and mention the name of Allah during known days over what He has provided them of cattle﴾ — Shu'bah [and Hushaym] [[Addition from F, A.]] narrated from [Abu Bishr, from Sa'id] [[Addition from F, A.]] from Ibn 'Abbas: "The known days are the days of the ten (first days of Dhu al-Hijjah)." Al-Bukhari transmitted it from him in a definitive form [[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/457), Fath.]]. The like of it is also related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. It is the view of al-Shafi'i, and the well-known position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "No deed is more beloved to Allah in any days than these [days]." They said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah?" He said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except a man who goes out risking his self and his wealth and does not return with anything."

It was also related by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (969), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2438), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (757), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1727).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan, gharib, sahih hadith. And on the subject there are reports from Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, and Jabir."

I say: I have thoroughly examined these chains and have devoted a separate volume to them [[He named it: "al-Ahadith al-Warida fi Fadl al-Ayyam al-'Ashr min Dhi al-Hijjah" (The Hadiths Related to the Virtue of the Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah).]]. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are no days greater before Allah, nor more beloved to Him for deeds performed in them, than these ten days. So increase in them in tahlil, takbir and tahmid." [[al-Musnad (2/75).]] It is also related by another route, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, with similar wording [[Related by Abu 'Awanah, as cited in Irwa' al-Ghalil (3/398) from al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, through Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Al-Bukhari said: "Ibn 'Umar and Abu Hurayrah used to go out to the market during the ten days and would glorify Allah (takbir), and the people would glorify Allah along with their takbir [[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/457), Fath.]]."

Ahmad also related from Jabir, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "This is the ten [days] by which Allah swore in His saying: ﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾ [al-Fajr: 1-2]." [[al-Musnad (3/327).]]

Some of the early scholars said: it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and We completed it with ten﴾ [al-A'raf: 142].

In Sunan Abi Dawud: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to fast these ten [days] [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2437).]].

These ten [days] include the Day of 'Arafah, concerning which it is established in Sahih Muslim from Abu Qatadah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about fasting the Day of 'Arafah, and he said: "I anticipate from Allah that it will expiate the sins of the previous year and the coming year." [[Sahih Muslim no. (1162), from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

And they include the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), which is the Greater Day of Hajj, and it has been reported in a hadith that it is the most excellent of days before Allah [[Related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/350) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (1765), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Qurt, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

In sum, it has been said that these ten [days] are the best days of the year, as the hadith states; many prefer them to the last ten days of Ramadan, because what is legislated in those (fasting, prayer, charity, and others) is legislated in these too, while these are distinguished by the obligation of performing the Hajj within them.

It has been said: the other [the last ten of Ramadan] is more excellent, because it includes the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), which is better than a thousand months.

Others took a middle position, saying: the days of these [ten] are more excellent, and the nights of that [Ramadan] are more excellent. By this the evidences are reconciled, and Allah knows best.

A second view regarding the known days: Qabus [the narrator] reported from Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The known days are the Day of Sacrifice and three days after it." This is also related from Ibn 'Umar and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal adopted it in one narration from him.

A third view: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to me: that Ibn 'Umar used to say: "The known days and the counted days together are four days: the known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the counted days are three days, the Day of Sacrifice [included]." This is a sound chain to him. It was also said by al-Suddi, and it is the view of Imam Malik ibn Anas. This view and the previous one are supported by His saying: ﴿over what He has provided them of cattle﴾, meaning: the mention of Allah at the time of slaughtering them.

A fourth view: they are the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and another day after it. This is the view of Abu Hanifah.

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from his father, that he said: "The known days are the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashriq."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿over what He has provided them of cattle﴾, it means: camels, cows and sheep, as He detailed them in Surah al-An'am, and that they are ﴿eight pairs﴾ [al-An'am: 143] and so on.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: whoever held that it is obligatory to eat from the sacrificial animals has used this verse as evidence, but this is a strange opinion. What most scholars hold is that it falls under permission or recommendation, as it is established that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered his offering, he ordered that a piece from every camel be cooked, so he ate from its meat and drank from its broth [[Related by Muslim in his Sahih no. (1218), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

'Abdullah ibn Wahb said: [Malik said to me: "I like that one eats from one's sacrifice, because Allah says: ﴿So eat from them﴾." Ibn Wahb said:] [[Addition from F, A.]] and I asked al-Layth, and he told me the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding ﴿So eat from them﴾: "The polytheists did not eat from their sacrifices, so it was permitted to the Muslims: whoever wishes eats, and whoever wishes does not eat." The like of this is also related from Mujahid and 'Ata'.

Hushaym said, from Husayn, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿So eat from them﴾: "It is like His saying: ﴿And when you are released [from ihram], then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10]."

This is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. Those who support the view that the sacrifices are to be divided into halves, with half given in charity, have used His saying in this verse: ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾, dividing it into two halves: one half for the one sacrificing and one half for the poor.

The other view is that it is divided into three parts: a third for himself, a third he gifts, and a third he gives in charity, based on His saying in the other verse: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [al-Hajj: 36]. The discussion of this will come at its place, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: 'Ikrimah said: "The miserable is the destitute who is afflicted with hardship, and the poor is the one who abstains from asking."

Mujahid said: "It is the one who does not extend his hand." Qatadah said: "It is the disabled." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "It is the blind."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Then let them end their untidiness﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is removing the ihram by shaving the head, wearing clothes, cutting the nails, and the like." 'Ata' and Mujahid related the same from him. Likewise said 'Ikrimah and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Then let them end their untidiness﴾: "The tafath is the rites (manasik)."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "It means slaughtering what one vowed of the camels."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: the vow of Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows of something that occurs in Hajj."

Ibrahim ibn Maysarah narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: the slaughtered animals."

Laith ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: every vow with a fixed term."

'Ikrimah said: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: their Hajj."

Likewise Imam Ibn Abi Hatim related: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us regarding His saying: ﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾, he said: "The vow of Hajj. Whoever enters Hajj, upon him is the work in it: circumambulating the House, between al-Safa and al-Marwah, 'Arafah, Muzdalifah, and throwing the pebbles, as they were commanded." The like of this is also related from Malik.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: Mujahid said: "It means the obligatory tawaf on the Day of Sacrifice."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah who said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "Do you recite Surah al-Hajj? Allah says: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾, for the last of the rites is the tawaf of the House."

I say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did likewise: when he returned to Mina on the Day of Sacrifice, he began by throwing the jamrah, throwing seven pebbles, then slaughtered his offering, shaved his head, then went forth and circumambulated the House. And in the Sahih, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "The people were commanded that the last of their dealings with the House be the tawaf, except that it was lightened for the menstruating woman [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (329) and Sahih Muslim no. (1328), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾: in it is evidence for those who hold that tawaf must be performed from behind the Hijr, because it is from the original House built by Ibrahim, although Quraysh had excluded it from the House when their expenses fell short. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated from behind the Hijr, and informed that the Hijr is part of the House, and he did not touch the two Syrian corners, because they were not completed upon the ancient foundations of Ibrahim. For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hujr, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated from behind it [[Also related by Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/41).]].

Qatadah narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri regarding His saying: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ [he said]: "Because it is the first House set up for mankind." Likewise said 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

It is related from 'Ikrimah that he said: "It was called the Ancient House because it was freed (u'tiqa) on the day of the Flood in the time of Nuh."

Khasif said: "It was called the Ancient House because no tyrant ever gained dominion over it."

Ibn Abi Najih and Layth narrated from Mujahid: "It was freed from the tyrants, so that they would not be given power over it." Qatadah said likewise.

Wa qala Hammad ibn Salamah, 'an Humayd, 'an al-Hasan ibn Muslim, 'an Mujahid: "Li-annahu lam yuridhu ahadun bi-su'in illa halak."

Wa qala 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'an Ma'mar, 'an al-Zuhri, 'an Ibn al-Zubayr, qala: "Innama summiya al-Bayt al-'Atiq li-anna Allah a'taqahu min al-jababirah" [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/32).]].

Wa qala al-Tirmidhi: Haddathana Muhammad ibn Isma'il wa ghayru wahid, haddathana 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, akhbarani al-Layth, 'an 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, 'an Ibn Shihab, 'an Muhammad ibn 'Urwah, 'an 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, qala: Qala Rasul Allah (ﷺ): "Innama summiya al-Bayt al-'Atiq li-annahu lam yazhar 'alayhi jabbar."

Wa kadha rawahu Ibn Jarir, 'an Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Naijari [[In (F): "al-Muharibi".]], 'an 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, bihi [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3170), and in it: "This is a hasan sahih hadith", and I think this is an error.]]. And he said: "In kana sahihan."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Then he narrated it through another route, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal report [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2654) and Sahih Muslim no. (87).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿that they may witness benefits for them﴾: "The benefits of this world and the Hereafter. As for the benefits of the Hereafter, they are the pleasure of Allah; and as for the benefits of this world, they are what they obtain of the benefits of the animals [[In T, F, A: "slaughtering" (al-dhaba'ih)]] , profit and trade." Likewise Mujahid and others said: "It refers to the benefits of this world and the Hereafter," like His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you seek bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 198].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and mention the name of Allah during known days over what He has provided them of cattle﴾ — Shu'bah [and Hushaym] [[Addition from F, A.]] narrated from [Abu Bishr, from Sa'id] [[Addition from F, A.]] from Ibn 'Abbas: "The known days are the days of the ten (first days of Dhu al-Hijjah)." Al-Bukhari transmitted it from him in a definitive form [[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/457), Fath.]]. The like of it is also related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. It is the view of al-Shafi'i, and the well-known position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "No deed is more beloved to Allah in any days than these [days]." They said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah?" He said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except a man who goes out risking his self and his wealth and does not return with anything."

It was also related by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (969), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2438), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (757), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1727).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan, gharib, sahih hadith. And on the subject there are reports from Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, and Jabir."

I say: I have thoroughly examined these chains and have devoted a separate volume to them [[He named it: "al-Ahadith al-Warida fi Fadl al-Ayyam al-'Ashr min Dhi al-Hijjah" (The Hadiths Related to the Virtue of the Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah).]]. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are no days greater before Allah, nor more beloved to Him for deeds performed in them, than these ten days. So increase in them in tahlil, takbir and tahmid." [[al-Musnad (2/75).]] It is also related by another route, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, with similar wording [[Related by Abu 'Awanah, as cited in Irwa' al-Ghalil (3/398) from al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, through Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Al-Bukhari said: "Ibn 'Umar and Abu Hurayrah used to go out to the market during the ten days and would glorify Allah (takbir), and the people would glorify Allah along with their takbir [[Sahih al-Bukhari (2/457), Fath.]]."

Ahmad also related from Jabir, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "This is the ten [days] by which Allah swore in His saying: ﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾ [al-Fajr: 1-2]." [[al-Musnad (3/327).]]

Some of the early scholars said: it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and We completed it with ten﴾ [al-A'raf: 142].

In Sunan Abi Dawud: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to fast these ten [days] [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2437).]].

These ten [days] include the Day of 'Arafah, concerning which it is established in Sahih Muslim from Abu Qatadah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about fasting the Day of 'Arafah, and he said: "I anticipate from Allah that it will expiate the sins of the previous year and the coming year." [[Sahih Muslim no. (1162), from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

And they include the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), which is the Greater Day of Hajj, and it has been reported in a hadith that it is the most excellent of days before Allah [[Related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/350) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (1765), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Qurt, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

In sum, it has been said that these ten [days] are the best days of the year, as the hadith states; many prefer them to the last ten days of Ramadan, because what is legislated in those (fasting, prayer, charity, and others) is legislated in these too, while these are distinguished by the obligation of performing the Hajj within them.

It has been said: the other [the last ten of Ramadan] is more excellent, because it includes the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), which is better than a thousand months.

Others took a middle position, saying: the days of these [ten] are more excellent, and the nights of that [Ramadan] are more excellent. By this the evidences are reconciled, and Allah knows best.

A second view regarding the known days: Qabus [the narrator] reported from Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The known days are the Day of Sacrifice and three days after it." This is also related from Ibn 'Umar and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal adopted it in one narration from him.

A third view: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to me: that Ibn 'Umar used to say: "The known days and the counted days together are four days: the known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the counted days are three days, the Day of Sacrifice [included]." This is a sound chain to him. It was also said by al-Suddi, and it is the view of Imam Malik ibn Anas. This view and the previous one are supported by His saying: ﴿over what He has provided them of cattle﴾, meaning: the mention of Allah at the time of slaughtering them.

A fourth view: they are the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and another day after it. This is the view of Abu Hanifah.

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from his father, that he said: "The known days are the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashriq."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿over what He has provided them of cattle﴾, it means: camels, cows and sheep, as He detailed them in Surah al-An'am, and that they are ﴿eight pairs﴾ [al-An'am: 143] and so on.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: whoever held that it is obligatory to eat from the sacrificial animals has used this verse as evidence, but this is a strange opinion. What most scholars hold is that it falls under permission or recommendation, as it is established that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered his offering, he ordered that a piece from every camel be cooked, so he ate from its meat and drank from its broth [[Related by Muslim in his Sahih no. (1218), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

'Abdullah ibn Wahb said: [Malik said to me: "I like that one eats from one's sacrifice, because Allah says: ﴿So eat from them﴾." Ibn Wahb said:] [[Addition from F, A.]] and I asked al-Layth, and he told me the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding ﴿So eat from them﴾: "The polytheists did not eat from their sacrifices, so it was permitted to the Muslims: whoever wishes eats, and whoever wishes does not eat." The like of this is also related from Mujahid and 'Ata'.

Hushaym said, from Husayn, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿So eat from them﴾: "It is like His saying: ﴿And when you are released [from ihram], then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10]."

This is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. Those who support the view that the sacrifices are to be divided into halves, with half given in charity, have used His saying in this verse: ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾, dividing it into two halves: one half for the one sacrificing and one half for the poor.

The other view is that it is divided into three parts: a third for himself, a third he gifts, and a third he gives in charity, based on His saying in the other verse: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [al-Hajj: 36]. The discussion of this will come at its place, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: 'Ikrimah said: "The miserable is the destitute who is afflicted with hardship, and the poor is the one who abstains from asking."

Mujahid said: "It is the one who does not extend his hand." Qatadah said: "It is the disabled." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "It is the blind."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Then let them end their untidiness﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is removing the ihram by shaving the head, wearing clothes, cutting the nails, and the like." 'Ata' and Mujahid related the same from him. Likewise said 'Ikrimah and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Then let them end their untidiness﴾: "The tafath is the rites (manasik)."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "It means slaughtering what one vowed of the camels."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: the vow of Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows of something that occurs in Hajj."

Ibrahim ibn Maysarah narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: the slaughtered animals."

Laith ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: every vow with a fixed term."

'Ikrimah said: "﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: their Hajj."

Likewise Imam Ibn Abi Hatim related: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us regarding His saying: ﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾, he said: "The vow of Hajj. Whoever enters Hajj, upon him is the work in it: circumambulating the House, between al-Safa and al-Marwah, 'Arafah, Muzdalifah, and throwing the pebbles, as they were commanded." The like of this is also related from Malik.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: Mujahid said: "It means the obligatory tawaf on the Day of Sacrifice."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah who said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "Do you recite Surah al-Hajj? Allah says: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾, for the last of the rites is the tawaf of the House."

I say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did likewise: when he returned to Mina on the Day of Sacrifice, he began by throwing the jamrah, throwing seven pebbles, then slaughtered his offering, shaved his head, then went forth and circumambulated the House. And in the Sahih, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "The people were commanded that the last of their dealings with the House be the tawaf, except that it was lightened for the menstruating woman [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (329) and Sahih Muslim no. (1328), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]."
* *
As for His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾: in it is evidence for those who hold that tawaf must be performed from behind the Hijr, because it is from the original House built by Ibrahim, although Quraysh had excluded it from the House when their expenses fell short. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated from behind the Hijr, and informed that the Hijr is part of the House, and he did not touch the two Syrian corners, because they were not completed upon the ancient foundations of Ibrahim. For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hujr, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated from behind it [[Also related by Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/41).]].

Ibn Abi Najih and Layth narrated from Mujahid: "It was freed from the tyrants, so that they would not be given power over it." Qatadah said likewise.

Wa qala Hammad ibn Salamah, 'an Humayd, 'an al-Hasan ibn Muslim, 'an Mujahid: "Li-annahu lam yuridhu ahadun bi-su'in illa halak."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Then he narrated it through another route, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal report [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2654) and Sahih Muslim no. (87).]].

Ibn Kathir said: This is what He commanded us of acts of obedience in performing the rites (manasik), and the abundant reward for the one who performs them.

﴿And whoever honours the sacred things of Allah﴾, i.e., whoever avoids His acts of disobedience and what He has forbidden, and regards committing them as grave in his own soul, ﴿it is better for him with his Lord﴾, i.e., he will have much good and a great reward for that. Just as there is a great reward and a large recompense for performing acts of obedience, so too there is for abandoning what is forbidden and for avoiding what is prohibited [ijtinab] [[Addition from manuscript A.]].

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said, concerning His words ﴿That, and whoever honours the sacred things of Allah﴾: "The sacred things are Makkah, the Hajj and the 'Umrah, and everything that Allah has forbidden of His acts of disobedience, all of them." Ibn Zayd also said the same.

* *

As for His words ﴿And the grazing livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you﴾, i.e., We have made lawful for you all grazing livestock, and Allah has not made any of them a bahirah, a sa'ibah, a wasilah, or a ham (the pre-Islamic practices of consecrating animals) [[In manuscript T: "Ahlalat" (it was made lawful).]].

* *

As for His words ﴿except what is recited to you﴾, i.e., of the prohibitions: ﴿Carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen from a height, the gored, and what has been eaten by a beast of prey, except what you have slaughtered properly﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:3]. This was stated by Ibn Jarir, who related it from Qatadah.

* *

As for His words ﴿So avoid the filth of idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾: here "min" (from) is for specification of the kind, meaning: avoid the filth which is the idols. He linked association with Allah (shirk) to "the word of falsehood," as in His words: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, sin, unjust transgression, your associating with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and your saying about Allah what you do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 7:33]. Among it is false testimony (shahadat al-zur).

In the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), it is related from Abu Bakrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating others with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He had been reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and the false word; beware, and false testimony." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would stop."

Imam Ahmad said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Ziyad informed us, from Fatik ibn Fadalah, from Ayman ibn Khuraym, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up to deliver a sermon and said: "O people, false testimony has been made equal to associating partners with Allah," three times. Then he recited: ﴿So avoid the filth of idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾.

Al-Tirmidhi related it in the same way from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah, with the same chain. Then he said: "It is gharib (singular). We only know it from the narration of Sufyan ibn Ziyad. It has been reported differently from him concerning this hadith, and we do not know of Ayman ibn Khuraym having heard from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Sufyan al-Usfuri narrated to us, from his father, from Habib ibn al-Nu'man al-Asadi, from Khuraym ibn Fatak al-Asadi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the dawn prayer, and when he had finished he stood up and said: "False testimony equals associating partners with Allah, mighty and majestic," then he recited this verse: ﴿So avoid the filth of idols and avoid the word of falsehood, being hanifs (upright, turning away from falsehood towards truth) for Allah, not associating anything with Him﴾.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Wa'il ibn Rabi'ah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: False testimony is equal to associating partners with Allah. Then he recited this verse.

* *

As for His words ﴿hunafa' lillah﴾ (upright for Allah), i.e., sincerely devoted to Him in religion, turning away from falsehood and directing themselves to the truth. For this reason He said ﴿not associating anything with Him﴾.

Then He gave the example of the polytheist in his misguidance, his ruin, and his distance from guidance, saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky﴾, i.e., dropped from it, ﴿and the birds snatch him away﴾, i.e., the birds tear him apart in the air, ﴿or the wind carries him off to a distant place﴾, i.e., a far place of destruction for whoever falls into it. For this reason, a hadith from al-Bara' says: "When the angels of death take the soul of the disbeliever and ascend with his spirit to the heaven, the gates of heaven are not opened for him; rather his spirit is cast down from there." Then he recited this verse. The hadith has already been mentioned in Surah Ibrahim [see the commentary on verse 27] with its wording, its phrasing, and its chains.

Allah the Exalted has given another example of the polytheist in Surah al-An'am, namely His words: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and be turned back upon our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have led astray in the earth, bewildered, who has companions calling him to guidance, saying: "Come to us." Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am 6:71] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A; in the original: "the verse".]].

Ibn Kathir said: This is what He commanded us of acts of obedience in performing the rites (manasik), and the abundant reward for the one who performs them.

﴿And whoever honours the sacred things of Allah﴾, i.e., whoever avoids His acts of disobedience and what He has forbidden, and regards committing them as grave in his own soul, ﴿it is better for him with his Lord﴾, i.e., he will have much good and a great reward for that. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Sufyan al-Usfuri narrated to us, from his father, from Habib ibn al-Nu'man al-Asadi, from Khuraym ibn Fatak al-Asadi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the dawn prayer, and when he had finished he stood up and said: "False testimony equals associating partners with Allah, mighty and majestic," then he recited this verse: ﴿So avoid the filth of idols and avoid the word of falsehood, being hanifs (upright, turning away from falsehood towards truth) for Allah, not associating anything with Him﴾.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Wa'il ibn Rabi'ah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: False testimony is equal to associating partners with Allah. Then he recited this verse.

* *

As for His words ﴿hunafa' lillah﴾ (upright for Allah), i.e., sincerely devoted to Him in religion, turning away from falsehood and directing themselves to the truth. For this reason He said ﴿not associating anything with Him﴾.

Then He gave the example of the polytheist in his misguidance, his ruin, and his distance from guidance, saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky﴾, i.e., dropped from it, ﴿and the birds snatch him away﴾, i.e., the birds tear him apart in the air, ﴿or the wind carries him off to a distant place﴾, i.e., a far place of destruction for whoever falls into it. For this reason, a hadith from al-Bara' says: "When the angels of death take the soul of the disbeliever and ascend with his spirit to the heaven, the gates of heaven are not opened for him; rather his spirit is cast down from there." Then he recited this verse. The hadith has already been mentioned in Surah Ibrahim [see the commentary on verse 27] with its wording, its phrasing, and its chains.

Allah the Exalted has given another example of the polytheist in Surah al-An'am, namely His words: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and be turned back upon our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have led astray in the earth, bewildered, who has companions calling him to guidance, saying: "Come to us." Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am 6:71] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A; in the original: "the verse".]].

Allah the Exalted says: "This" and "whoever honours the symbols of Allah" ﴿وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾, meaning His commands, "indeed it is from the piety of hearts" ﴿فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ﴾. Among this is honouring the offerings (hadaya, animals brought to Makkah for sacrifice) and the camels (budn). Al-Hakam narrated from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: honouring them means fattening them and choosing good ones.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿That, and whoever honours the symbols of Allah﴾, he said: "It is fattening, choosing the best, and esteeming them greatly."

Abu Umamah ibn Sahl said: "We used to fatten the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) in Madinah, and the Muslims would fatten theirs." Al-Bukhari narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari (10/9), Fath, as a mu'allaq (suspended narration)].

From Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of an 'afra' (a white-spotted or light-coloured animal) is more beloved to Allah than the blood of two black ones." Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated it [al-Musnad (2/417); I have not found it in Sunan Ibn Majah].

They said: "The 'afra' is the white, but not pure white. The white is better than others, and others are also valid, because it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two horned rams, white with black markings (amlahayn)." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5558.]

From Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed a horned ram, a stallion (fahl) [in F: "fahl"], which walked, looked and ate in blackness, meaning a black ram in those places. The people of the Sunan narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2796; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1496; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/221); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3128. In A: "it has a black spot"].

In Sunan Ibn Majah, from Abu Rafi', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two large, fat, horned, white-with-black-markings rams that were castrated (mawjU'ayn) [This does not occur in Sunan Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abu Rafi'; rather it is from the hadith of Aishah and Abu Hurayrah, no. 3122, and the hadith of Abu Rafi' is narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/8)]. It was said: they are the castrated ones; and it was said: those whose testicles were crushed but not cut off. And Allah knows best.

Likewise Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from Jabir: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two horned, white-with-black-markings, castrated rams [and "mawjU'ayn" was said to mean the castrated]. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2795.]

From Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to look for the eye and the ear (to be sound), and not to sacrifice one with a cut at the front of the ear (muqabalah), nor one with a cut at the back (mudabarah), nor one with a split lengthwise (sharqa'), nor one with a round hole (kharqa')."

Ahmad and the people of the Sunan narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it [al-Musnad (1/80); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2804; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1498; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/217); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3142].

They also narrated from him: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade sacrificing one whose horn or ear was broken off (a'adb)." [al-Musnad (1/83); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2805; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1504; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/217); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3145. In T: "yudahhi".]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "al-'adb" is half or more.

Some lexicographers said: if the upper horn is broken, it is qasma'; as for 'adb, it is the breaking of the lower part, and 'adab al-udhn is the cutting of part of the ear.

According to al-Shafi'i, sacrificing with such an animal is valid but disliked.

Ahmad said: a sacrifice with an animal whose horn or ear is broken is not valid, because of this hadith.

Malik said: if blood flows from the horn, it is not valid; otherwise it is valid. And Allah knows best.

As for al-Muqabalah, it is the animal whose front of the ear is cut off; al-Mudabarah is the one whose back of the ear is cut off. Al-Sharqa' is the one whose ear is cut lengthwise, as al-Shafi'i said. Al-Kharqa' is the one whose ear has been pierced by the branding mark in a round hole. And Allah knows best.

From al-Bara', who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four are not permitted in sacrificial animals: the one-eyed whose blindness is evident, the sick whose sickness is evident, the lame whose limping is evident, and the emaciated that has no marrow." [In T and A: "its lameness".]

Ahmad and the people of the Sunan narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it [al-Musnad (4/284); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2802; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1497; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/215); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3144].

These defects reduce the meat, because of the animal's weakness and its inability to complete grazing, since the sheep overtake them to the pasture. Therefore sacrificing with them is not valid according to al-Shafi'i and other imams, as is the apparent meaning of the hadith.

Al-Shafi'i's opinion differed regarding an animal with a slight illness, with two views.

Abu Dawud narrated from Utbah ibn Abd al-Sulami that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the musfirah, the musta'salah, the bakhqa', the mushayya'ah, and the kasra'. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2803; in A: "al-kasrah".]

Al-Musfirah is said to be the emaciated one; and it is said that al-Musta'salah is the one whose ear is cut off entirely. Al-Mustasalah is the one whose horn is broken. Al-Bakhqa' is the one-eyed. Al-Mushayyi'ah is the one that always trails behind the flock and does not follow, due to its weakness. Al-Kasra' is the lame.

All these defects prevent validity. If a defect appears after the sacrificial animal has been designated, then according to al-Shafi'i its defect does not harm it, unlike Abu Hanifah's view.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: "I bought a ram to sacrifice, and a wolf came and took its tail (alyah). I asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Sacrifice it.'" [al-Musnad (3/32).]

For this reason, the hadith says: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to look for the eye and the ear," meaning: the hadi or the udhiyah should be fat, good and valuable, as Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: "Umar gave a noble camel as a gift, and he was offered three hundred dinars for it. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I gave a noble camel as a gift, and I was offered three hundred dinars for it. Shall I sell it and buy with its price other camels?' He said: 'No, sacrifice it instead.'" [al-Musnad (2/145); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1756.]

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas: "The camels are among the symbols of Allah."

Muhammad ibn Abi Musa said: "Standing at 'Arafat, Muzdalifah, the stoning of the pillars (jimar), the throwing, the camels, and the shaving are among the symbols of Allah."

Ibn Umar said: "The greatest of the symbols is the House."

His words: ﴿For you therein are benefits﴾, meaning: for you in the camels are benefits: from their milk, their wool, their fleece and hair, and riding them.

﴿until a specified term﴾: Miqsam narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿For you therein are benefits until a specified term﴾, he said: "As long as it has not been designated as a camel for sacrifice (budn)."

Mujahid said regarding His words ﴿For you therein are benefits until a specified term﴾: "Riding, milk, and offspring. When it is designated as a badanah or a hady, all of that ends." Likewise said Ata', al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil, Ata' al-Khurasani, and others.

Others said: rather, he may benefit from it even if it is a hady, when he needs to, as is established in the two Sahihs from Anas: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a man driving a camel, and he said: "Ride it." He said: "It is a camel for sacrifice." He said: "Ride it, woe to you," on the second or third time. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1690; Sahih Muslim no. 1323.]

In a narration of Muslim, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Ride it in a reasonable manner when you are compelled to it." [Sahih Muslim no. 1323.]

Shu'bah said, from Zuhayr ibn Abi Thabit al-A'ma, from al-Mughirah ibn Hudhf, from Ali: that he saw a man driving a camel with its calf, and said: "Do not drink from its milk except what is surplus to its calf. When the Day of Sacrifice comes, slaughter it and its calf."

* *

His words: ﴿Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, meaning: the place of the hady and its end is at the Ancient House, which is the Ka'bah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95], and He said: ﴿and the offering detained from reaching its place of sacrifice﴾ [al-Fath: 25].

The discussion of the meaning of "the Ancient House" has been mentioned earlier, and praise is to Allah. [In T: "And Allah knows best."]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah al-Hajj, verses 34–35:

He, exalted is He, informs that the slaughter of sacrifices (al-manasik) and the shedding of blood in the name of Allah has always been prescribed in all the religious communities (al-milal).

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾ that he said: "A festival (ʿid)."

'Ikrimah said: "A slaughter (dhabh)." Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His words ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite﴾: "It is Makkah. Allah never appointed a rite for any community other than it."

[And His words] ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over the cattle He has provided for them﴾ — as is established in the two Sahihs from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought two horned rams, white with black markings, and he pronounced the name of Allah and said takbir, and he placed his foot on their necks" (al-Bukhari, no. 5558; Muslim, no. 1966).

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Salam ibn Miskin informed us, from 'A'idh Allah al-Mujashi'i, from Abu Dawud (and he is Nufay' ibn al-Harith), from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I said — or they said — 'O Messenger of Allah, what are these sacrifices (al-adahi)?' He said: 'The Sunnah of your father Ibrahim.' They said: 'What do we get from them?' He said: 'For every hair, a good deed.' They said: 'And the wool?' He said: 'For every hair of the wool, a good deed.'"

Ibn Majah, Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid, also recorded it in his Sunan from the hadith of Salam ibn Miskin, with its chain (al-Musnad, 4/368).

* *

As for His words ﴿So your God is one God, so submit to Him﴾: meaning, your object of worship is one, even though the laws of the prophets varied and some abrogated others (naskh). All of them call to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. Therefore He said: ﴿so submit to Him﴾, meaning: devote yourselves sincerely and surrender to His judgment and obedience.

﴿And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin)﴾: Mujahid said: "The reassured (al-mutma'innin)." Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: "The humble (al-mutawadi'in)." Al-Suddi said: "The fearful (al-wajilin)." 'Amr ibn Aws said: "Al-mukhbitun are those who do not wrong, and when they are wronged, they do not seek retribution."

al-Thawri said regarding ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾: "Those who are reassured, content with Allah's decree, and submissive to Him."

The best explanation of it is by what follows it, which is His words ﴿those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾, meaning their hearts fear Him, ﴿and the patient over what befalls them﴾, meaning of calamities.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By Allah, you will either be patient or you will perish."

﴿And the establishers of prayer (al-muqimi al-salah)﴾: The majority of readers recited it with the genitive construction (idafah), as did the seven and the rest of the ten. Ibn al-Sumayqa' also read "wal-muqimina al-salah" with the accusative.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The nun (of al-muqimina) is dropped here for lightness; if it were dropped for the idafah, the word al-salah would have to be in the genitive, but it is in the accusative for the sake of lightness."

That is: those who fulfill Allah's right in performing the obligations He has enjoined upon them. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾, meaning they spend from the good provision Allah has given them on their families, their slaves, their relatives, their poor and needy, and they show kindness to the creatures of Allah while safeguarding the limits of Allah. These attributes are the opposite of the attributes of the hypocrites, for they are the reverse of all this, as has already been explained in Surah al-Tawbah [see the commentary on verse 67].
