'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾ that he said: "A festival (ʿid)."

'Ikrimah said: "A slaughter (dhabh)." Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His words ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite﴾: "It is Makkah. Allah never appointed a rite for any community other than it."

[And His words] ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over the cattle He has provided for them﴾ — as is established in the two Sahihs from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought two horned rams, white with black markings, and he pronounced the name of Allah and said takbir, and he placed his foot on their necks" (al-Bukhari, no. 5558; Muslim, no. 1966).

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Salam ibn Miskin informed us, from 'A'idh Allah al-Mujashi'i, from Abu Dawud (and he is Nufay' ibn al-Harith), from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I said — or they said — 'O Messenger of Allah, what are these sacrifices (al-adahi)?' He said: 'The Sunnah of your father Ibrahim.' They said: 'What do we get from them?' He said: 'For every hair, a good deed.' They said: 'And the wool?' He said: 'For every hair of the wool, a good deed.'"

Ibn Majah, Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid, also recorded it in his Sunan from the hadith of Salam ibn Miskin, with its chain (al-Musnad, 4/368).

* *

As for His words ﴿So your God is one God, so submit to Him﴾: meaning, your object of worship is one, even though the laws of the prophets varied and some abrogated others (naskh). All of them call to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. Therefore He said: ﴿so submit to Him﴾, meaning: devote yourselves sincerely and surrender to His judgment and obedience.

﴿And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin)﴾: Mujahid said: "The reassured (al-mutma'innin)." Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: "The humble (al-mutawadi'in)." Al-Suddi said: "The fearful (al-wajilin)." 'Amr ibn Aws said: "Al-mukhbitun are those who do not wrong, and when they are wronged, they do not seek retribution."

al-Thawri said regarding ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾: "Those who are reassured, content with Allah's decree, and submissive to Him."

The best explanation of it is by what follows it, which is His words ﴿those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾, meaning their hearts fear Him, ﴿and the patient over what befalls them﴾, meaning of calamities.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By Allah, you will either be patient or you will perish."

﴿And the establishers of prayer (al-muqimi al-salah)﴾: The majority of readers recited it with the genitive construction (idafah), as did the seven and the rest of the ten. Ibn al-Sumayqa' also read "wal-muqimina al-salah" with the accusative.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The nun (of al-muqimina) is dropped here for lightness; if it were dropped for the idafah, the word al-salah would have to be in the genitive, but it is in the accusative for the sake of lightness."

That is: those who fulfill Allah's right in performing the obligations He has enjoined upon them. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾, meaning they spend from the good provision Allah has given them on their families, their slaves, their relatives, their poor and needy, and they show kindness to the creatures of Allah while safeguarding the limits of Allah. These attributes are the opposite of the attributes of the hypocrites, for they are the reverse of all this, as has already been explained in Surah al-Tawbah [see the commentary on verse 67].

He, may He be exalted, says, reminding His servants of the favour He has bestowed on them through the camels [budn] He created for them, and that He made them among His rites (sha'a'ir, the symbols of God's worship). Namely, He made them to be brought as offerings (hady) to His Sacred House. Indeed, they are the best of what is brought [to His Sacred House], [[Addition from A.]] as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the garlands, nor those making for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His good pleasure﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 2], and so on.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' said concerning His words, ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the rites of God﴾, that they are the cow and the camel. This was also related from Ibn 'Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Mujahid said: The budn are only from the camels.

I say: As for applying the term badanah (camel for sacrifice) to the camel, there is agreement. The scholars differed over whether the term badanah may be applied to the cow, in two opinions. The more correct of them is that it is applied to it by the Law, as is established in the hadith.

Then the majority of scholars hold that a camel (badanah) suffices for seven and a cow suffices for seven, as is established by the hadith in Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah [and others], who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ commanded us to share in the sacrifices: a camel is for seven, and a cow is for seven. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1318.]]

[Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and others said: Rather, a cow suffices for seven and a camel for ten.] [[Addition from F, A.]] A hadith to this effect has come in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Sunan of al-Nasa'i, and others, [[The Musnad (1/275) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/222), from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ on a journey, and the day of sacrifice arrived, so we shared in a camel for ten and a cow for seven."]] So God knows best.

* *

His words, ﴿For you therein is good﴾: that is, reward in the Hereafter.

From Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Ka'bi, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No deed performed by the son of Adam on the day of sacrifice is more beloved to God than shedding blood. On the Day of Resurrection it will come with its horns, hooves and hair, and the blood will fall in a place with God before it falls on the earth, so be content with it." Narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1493; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3126.]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Hatim [[In A: "Abu Hazim".]] used to borrow money in order to drive the budn. It was said to him: "You borrow and drive the budn?" He said: "I heard God say: ﴿For you therein is good﴾."

From Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Silver has not been spent on anything better than a sacrifice (nahirah) on a day of festival." Narrated by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan. [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (4/282), by way of Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Mujahid said concerning ﴿For you therein is good﴾: reward and benefits.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: He rides it and milks it when he is in need of it.

* *

His words, ﴿So mention the name of God over them, standing in ranks﴾: From [al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn HanTab, from] [[Addition from F, A.]] Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I prayed with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the festival of Eid al-Adha. When he finished, a ram was brought to him, and he slaughtered it, saying: "In the name of God, and God is greatest. O God, this is from me and from whoever among my ummah did not sacrifice." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi. [[The Musnad (3/356); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2810; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1521. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith from this route."]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sacrificed two rams on the day of Eid. When he turned them [toward the qiblah], he said: "I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, as a true monotheist (hanif), a Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner, and I have been commanded to this, and I am the first of the Muslims. O God, it is from You and to You, and on behalf of Muhammad and his ummah." Then he mentioned God's name, said takbir, and slaughtered. [[The takhrij of this hadith was mentioned in the commentary on verse 162 of Surat al-An'am.]]

From 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Rafi', that the Messenger of God ﷺ, when he sacrificed, would buy two fat, horned, white-and-black rams. When he had prayed and addressed the people, one of them was brought to him while he was standing in his place of prayer, and he slaughtered it himself with the knife, then said: "O God, this is on behalf of my whole ummah, for whoever bore witness to You with monotheism and bore witness to me with the delivery of the message." Then the other was brought, and he slaughtered it himself, then said: "This is on behalf of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad." Then he would give both to the poor to eat, and he and his family would eat from them. Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Majah. [[The Musnad (6/8); the hadith was mentioned earlier in this surah.]]

al-A'mash said, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, ﴿So mention the name of God over them, standing in ranks﴾, that it means: standing on three legs, with its left foreleg tied, and he says: "In the name of God, and God is greatest [[In F, A: "and God is greatest, there is no god but God".]], O God, from You and to You." Similarly, Mujahid, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas something similar.

Al-Layth said, from Mujahid: If its left leg is tied, it stands on three. Ibn Abi Najih related from him something similar.

al-Dahhak said: One leg is tied so that it stands on three.

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar: that he passed by a man who had made his budnah kneel and was slaughtering it, and he said: "Make it stand, tied, the Sunnah of Abu al-Qasim ﷺ." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1713; Sahih Muslim, no. 1320.]]

From Jabir: that the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions used to slaughter the budn with the left [foreleg] tied, standing on what remained of its legs. Narrated by Abu Dawud. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1767.]]

Ibn Lahi'ah said: 'Ata' ibn Dinar told me that Salim ibn 'Abd Allah said to Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik: "Stand on its right side, and slaughter from its left side."

In Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, in describing the Farewell Pilgrimage, he said in it: The Messenger of God ﷺ slaughtered sixty-three budn with his own hand, [and] he would stab them with a spear in his hand. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1218.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "ṣawafin", meaning tied, standing. [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/33).]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Mujahid: Whoever reads it "ṣawafin", he said: tied. And whoever reads it ﴿ṣawaff﴾, he said: they are arranged in rows before them.

Tawus, al-Hasan and others said: "So mention the name of God over them, ṣawafiya", meaning: sincere, purely for God, Mighty and Majestic. Malik also related it similarly from al-Zuhri.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "ṣawafiya": there is no shirk in them like the shirk of the Jahiliyyah with their idols.

* *

His words, ﴿Then when their sides fall (wajabat junubuha)﴾: Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: It means: they fall to the ground.

This is also a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿when their sides fall﴾ means: they are slaughtered.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿when their sides fall﴾ means: they die.

This last view is the meaning intended by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid, for it is not permissible to eat from a budnah that has been slaughtered until it dies and its movement has ceased. There has come in a marfu' hadith: "Do not hasten the souls to depart." [[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (4/283), by way of Sa'id ibn Salam al-'Attar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Badil, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, as a marfu' report. Sa'id ibn Salam al-'Attar was declared a liar by Ahmad and Ibn Numayr, and al-Bayhaqi weakened this hadith in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/278).]] It was also related by al-Thawri in his Jami', from Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Furafisah al-Hanafi, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he said this. [[It was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/278) by way of al-Thawri.]] It is supported by the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws in Sahih Muslim: "God has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well; let each of you sharpen his blade and ease the suffering of his animal." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1955.]]

From Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whatever is cut from a beast while it is alive is carrion." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it. [[The Musnad (5/218); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2858; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1480.]]

* *

His words, ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: Some of the early scholars [[In A: "people".]] said: His words ﴿So eat from them﴾ are a command of permission.

Malik said: It is recommended. Others said: It is obligatory. This is also a view of some Shafi'is. Differences arose concerning the meaning of al-qani' (the contented) and al-mu'tarr (the beggar). al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: al-qani' is the one who is content with what you give him, and he is at home. And al-mu'tarr is the one who presents himself to you and approaches you, desiring that you give him some meat, and does not ask. Likewise said Mujahid and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: al-qani' is the one who abstains (al-mutaaffif), and al-mu'tarr is the one who asks. This is the view of Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Mujahid in one report from him.

Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn Aslam, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn al-Kalbi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Malik ibn Anas said: al-qani' is the one who approaches you and asks you. And al-mu'tarr is the one who comes to you, humbly, and does not ask you. This is the wording of al-Hasan.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-qani' is the one who asks. Then he said: Have you not heard the words of al-Shammakh?

"The wealth of a man, which sets him right and makes him sufficient for his needs, is more chaste than begging (al-qunu')."

He said: meaning from askers. Ibn Zayd said likewise.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: al-qani' is the poor man who goes around (for begging). And al-mu'tarr is the friend and the guest who visits. This is also a report from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd.

From Mujahid also: al-qani' is your rich neighbour who sees what enters your house, and al-mu'tarr is the one who comes to you from among the people.

And from him: that al-qani' is the one who is greedy, and al-mu'tarr is the one who presents himself with the budn, whether rich or poor.

Similar to this is related from 'Ikrimah, and from him: al-qani' is the people of Makkah.

Ibn Jarir preferred that al-qani' is the one who asks, because he is called qani' when he raises his hand for asking, and al-mu'tarr is from i'tirar, which is the one who presents himself to eat the meat.

Those scholars who held that the sacrifice is divided into three parts have used this noble verse as evidence: one third for its owner to eat, one third to give as gifts to his companions, and one third to give in charity to the poor, because He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾. In the authentic hadith, the Messenger of God ﷺ said to the people: "I had forbidden you to store the meat of the sacrifices beyond three days, so eat and store what you wish." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 977, from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may God be pleased with him.]] And in another narration: "So eat, store, and give in charity." And in another narration: "So eat, feed others, and give in charity." [[Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta' (2/484) from the hadith of Jabir, may God be pleased with him.]]

The second opinion: the one sacrificing eats half and gives away half, based on His words in the previous verse, ﴿So eat from it and feed the distressed, the poor﴾ [al-Hajj: 28], and on His words in the hadith: "Eat, store, and give in charity."

If he eats all of it, it is said: he owes nothing for it. This was the view of Ibn Suraij from the Shafi'is.

Some of them said: he must compensate for all of it, with its equivalent or its value. It was also said: he must compensate for half of it. It was said: a third of it. It was said: the least portion of it. This is the well-known position of the school of al-Shafi'i.

As for the hides, in Musnad Ahmad, from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, in the hadith about sacrificial animals: "Eat and give in charity, benefit from their hides, and do not sell them." [Musnad (4/15).]

Some scholars granted a concession regarding this [added in some manuscripts], and some of them said: he should share their price with the poor, and Allah knows best.

[Issue.]

From al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then return and slaughter. Whoever does this has followed our Sunnah, and whoever slaughters before the prayer, it is merely meat [he has hastened] for his family, and has nothing to do with the rite (nusuk) at all." [Added from some manuscripts and from al-Bukhari: in one manuscript, "he has started it".] Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5545); Sahih Muslim, no. (1961).]

Therefore al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars said: the beginning of the time for the Eid sacrifice is when the sun rises on the Day of Sacrifice and the time needed for the Eid prayer and the two sermons has passed. Ahmad added: and that the imam should slaughter first, based on what is in Sahih Muslim: "And do not slaughter until the imam has slaughtered." [I have not come across this wording in Muslim; see Sahih Muslim (3/1551).]

Abu Hanifah said: As for the people of the countryside (ahl al-sawad) and similar places, they may slaughter after dawn, since there is no Eid prayer for them in his view. As for the people of the major cities (al-amsar), they must not slaughter until the imam has prayed. And Allah knows best.

Then it was said: slaughtering is prescribed only on the Day of Sacrifice alone. It was said: the Day of Sacrifice applies to the people of the cities, because sacrificial animals are easily available to them, while for the people of the countryside it is the Day of Sacrifice and the days of tashriq (the days of drying meat, after the Day of Sacrifice). This was the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was said: the Day of Sacrifice and one day after it for everyone. It was said: the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and this was the view of Ahmad. It was said: the Day of Sacrifice and the three days of tashriq after it, and this was the view of al-Shafi'i, based on the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All the days of tashriq are days of slaughter." Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. [Musnad (4/82).]

It was also said: the time for slaughter extends to the end of Dhu al-Hijjah. This was the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. This is a rare (gharib) opinion.

* *

His words: ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may give thanks﴾. He, exalted is He, says: For this reason, ﴿We have subjected them to you﴾, that is, We have made them submissive to you, tamed and obedient. If you wish, you may ride them; if you wish, you may milk them; if you wish, you may slaughter them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not see that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. And for them in them are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71-73]. And in this noble verse He said: ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may give thanks﴾.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah, the Exalted, says: "He has only prescribed for you the slaughter of these sacrificial animals (hadaya) and offerings (dahaya), so that you mention His name when slaughtering them, for He is the Creator and the Provider [[In manuscripts T and F: "al-Razzaq"]], not that anything of their meat or blood reaches Him, for He, the Exalted, is free of need from all else."

In their pre-Islamic ignorance (jahiliyyah), when they slaughtered these animals for their idols, they would place some of their meat upon them and sprinkle some of their blood on them. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Their meat does not reach Allah, nor does their blood, but it is your piety that reaches Him.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: The people of the jahiliyyah used to sprinkle the House (the Ka'bah) with the meat and blood of camels. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have more right to sprinkle it." So Allah revealed: ﴿Their meat does not reach Allah, nor does their blood, but it is your piety that reaches Him﴾, meaning: He accepts that and rewards for it.

As has come in the Sahih: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms [[In T and F: "your colours"]] or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2564.]]

And what has come in the hadith: "Indeed, charity falls into the hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the beggar, and indeed the blood falls from Allah at a place before it falls upon the earth," as the hadith has already been mentioned. It was narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, from Aisha, raised to the Prophet. Its meaning is that it is intended to establish acceptance from Allah for whoever is sincere in his deed, and there is no other meaning that comes to mind among the verifying scholars, besides this. And Allah knows best.

Waki' said, from Yahya [[Added from T]] ibn Muslim Abu al-Dahhak: I asked Amir al-Sha'bi about the hides of the sacrificial animals, and he said: ﴿Their meat does not reach Allah, nor does their blood﴾; if you wish, sell them; if you wish, keep them; and if you wish, give them in charity.

* *

His saying: ﴿Thus He subjected them to you﴾, meaning: for this reason He subjected the camels (budn) to you, ﴿that you may glorify Allah for having guided you﴾, meaning: that you may magnify Him for guiding you to His religion, His law, what He loves and what He is pleased with, and for forbidding you from doing what He dislikes and rejects.

* *

His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the doers of good﴾, meaning: and give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the doers of good, that is, in their deeds, those who uphold the limits of Allah, who follow what He has legislated for them, and who affirm the Messenger in what he conveyed to them and brought to them from their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

[Issue] [[Added from F]]

Abu Hanifah, Malik and al-Thawri held the view that sacrifice (udhiyyah) is obligatory for whoever possesses the minimum wealth (nisab). Abu Hanifah additionally required residence (iqamah). They argued with what Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated with a chain whose narrators are all trustworthy, from Abu Hurairah, raised: "Whoever finds the means and does not sacrifice, let him not come near our prayer-place." [[Musnad, 2/321; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3123. In its chain is Abdullah ibn Ayyash. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/50): "Although Muslim narrated from him, he narrated only in supporting and corroborating reports. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i declared him weak, Abu Hatim and Ibn Yunus said he was munkar al-hadith, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy." He then cited al-Bayhaqi, who reported from al-Tirmidhi that the sound version from Abu Hurairah is mawquf (stopping at the Companion). End.
It may be answered that this hadith does not indicate obligation, as in the hadith: "Whoever eats garlic, let him not come near our prayer-place." Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned this, and there the disapproval is not necessarily rejected.]]

Ibn Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained for ten years offering sacrifice. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1507, and he graded it hasan.]]

Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad said: Sacrifice is not obligatory, rather it is recommended (mustahabb), based on what has come in the hadith: "There is no right in wealth other than zakah." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1789, from the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, may Allah be pleased with her.]] It has already been mentioned that he (peace be upon him) sacrificed on behalf of his ummah, and that this removed its obligation from them.

Abu Suraihah said: I was a neighbour of Abu Bakr and Umar, and they would not sacrifice, out of fear that people would follow their example.

Some people said: Sacrifice is a collective sunnah (sunnat kifayah): if one person from a household or a neighbourhood performs it, it is dropped from the rest, because the purpose is to display the rites (shi'ar).

Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated, and al-Tirmidhi graded it hasan, from Mikhnaf ibn Sulaim, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say at Arafat: "For every household, every year, there is an udhiyyah and an 'atirah. Do you know what the 'atirah is? It is what you call the Rajabiyyah." Its chain has been criticised. [[Musnad, 4/125; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2788; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1518; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 7/167; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3125.]]

Abu Ayyub said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man would sacrifice one sheep on behalf of himself and his household; they would eat and feed others, until people began to boast, and it became as you see.

Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sahih, and by Ibn Majah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1505; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3147.]]

Abdullah ibn Hisham used to sacrifice one sheep on behalf of all his family. Narrated by al-Bukhari.

As for the minimum age of the sacrificial animal, Muslim narrated from Jabir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not slaughter except a musinnah (an adult animal), unless it is difficult for you, in which case slaughter a jadha'ah (young animal) of sheep." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1963.]]

From here, al-Zuhri held that a jadha'ah is not sufficient. Al-Awza'i opposed him and held that a jadha'ah is sufficient from every kind, and both views are rare. The majority said: Only the thaniyy (the adult) of camels, cattle and goats is sufficient, and the jadha' of sheep. The thaniyy of camels is the one that has completed five years and entered its sixth. Of cattle, it is the one that has two years and has entered its third; it was said: the one that has three years and has entered its fourth. Of goats, it is the one that has two years. As for the jadha' of sheep, it was said: the one that has one year; it was said: ten months; it was said: eight months; it was said: six months, and this is the least of what has been said about its age. Anything below that is a hamal (lamb). The difference between them is that the hamal's back hair stands upright, while the jadha''s back hair lies flat, having become even in its two tusks (or teeth). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 22, verse 38:

He, exalted is He, informs that He repels from His servants who rely upon Him and turn back to Him the evil of the most evil and the plotting of the wicked. He protects them, watches over them, and gives them victory, as He says: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36] And He says: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Certainly, Allah has set a measure for all things.﴾ [at-Talaq: 3]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ingrate.﴾ That is: He does not love, from among His servants, whoever is characterized by this, namely treachery in covenants and pledges, not fulfilling what he has said. And al-kufr [[In manuscript T: "wal-kafur".]]: denial of blessings, so that one does not acknowledge them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verses 39–40:

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: It was revealed concerning Muhammad and his companions when they were expelled from Makkah.

Many of the early generations (al-salaf) said[[In MSS F and A: "Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said."]]: This is the first verse revealed concerning jihad. Some scholars also used this verse as evidence that the surah is Madani (revealed in Madinah). This was said by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to me: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Muslim (that is, al-Batin), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was expelled from Makkah, Abu Bakr said: "They have expelled their Prophet! Surely we belong to Allah and to Him we shall return, [and they will be destroyed]." Ibn 'Abbas said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Permission [to fight] is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged; and indeed, Allah is able to give them victory.﴾ Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Then I knew that there would be fighting."[[In MS F: "Abu Bakr" is given without the honorific here.]]

Ahmad also related it from Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq, with the same chain, and added: Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is the first verse revealed about fighting."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir, from their Sunan, and Ibn Abi Hatim[[In MS T: "Ibn Majah."]], narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yusuf (al-Tirmidhi added: and Waki', both of them from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain). al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan hadith. It has been narrated by more than one from al-Thawri, and in it there is no mention of Ibn 'Abbas."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3171; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. 11345.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is able to give them victory﴾ means: He is capable of granting victory to His believing servants without fighting. But He wants His servants to exert their utmost effort in obeying Him, as He said: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, bind them firmly, and then either [release them] as a favor or ransom until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordains fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — He will never waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition and admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them.﴾ [Muhammad: 4–6]. He also said: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the hearts of a believing people. And remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14–15]. And He said: ﴿Or do you think that you will be left [alone] while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strove and did not take other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 16]. ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought [in His way] and made evident those who are patient?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142]. And He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We make evident those of you who strive and are patient, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad: 31].

The verses on this are many. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed, Allah is able to give them victory﴾: "And He has done so."

Allah, Exalted, legislated jihad at the most fitting time for it. When they were in Makkah, the polytheists were far greater in number. Had the Muslims, who were fewer than a tenth of them, been commanded to fight the rest, it would have been hard for them. For this reason, when the people of Yathrib (Madinah) pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of al-'Aqabah, and they were a little over eighty, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not swoop down upon the people of the valley (meaning the people of Mina) during the nights of Mina and kill them?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have not been commanded to do this." Then, when the polytheists transgressed, expelled the Prophet ﷺ from among them, plotted to kill him, and scattered his companions in every direction, some of them went to Abyssinia and others to Madinah. When they settled in Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ joined them, they gathered around him, stood by his support, and it became for them an abode of Islam and a stronghold to which they could turn, then Allah legislated the jihad against the enemies. This verse was the first thing revealed about that. He, Exalted, said: ﴿Permission [to fight] is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged; and indeed, Allah is able to give them victory. [They are] those who have been expelled from their homes without right﴾.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: They were expelled from Makkah to Madinah without right, meaning Muhammad and his companions.

﴿Only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾: that is, they had done no wrong to their people and had committed no sin, except that they worshipped Allah alone, without partner. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati') with respect to the reality of the matter. But in the view of the polytheists it is the greatest of sins, as He said: ﴿They expel the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord.﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1]. He, Exalted, also said regarding the people of the trench: ﴿And they resented them only because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.﴾ [al-Buruj: 8]. For this reason, when the Muslims were chanting verses while digging the trench, saying:

"O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided,
Nor would we have given charity or prayed.
So send down tranquility upon us,
And make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy].
Indeed, those who have transgressed against us,
When they desire strife, we refuse."[[These verses are attributed to 'Amir ibn al-Akwa' as in Sahih Muslim, no. 1803.]]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would join them and say the last word of each line with them. When they said, "When they desire strife, we refuse," he would say "We refuse," prolonging his voice with it.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another﴾, that is: were it not that He repels [harm] from one people by means of another and averts the evil of some people from others, through the causes He creates and decrees, the earth would have been corrupted, and the strong would have destroyed the weak.

﴿Surely would have been demolished monasteries﴾, which are the small places of worship for monks. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and others.

Qatadah said: They are the places of worship of the Sabians. In another report from him: the monasteries of the Magians (Majus).

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They are the houses that are on the roads.

﴿And churches﴾: these are larger than those, and more worshippers gather in them. They also belong to the Christians. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Sakhr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Khusayf and others.

Ibn Jubayr related from Mujahid and others that they are the synagogues of the Jews. al-Suddi related, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that they are the synagogues of the Jews. Mujahid only said: "They are the churches." And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And monasteries﴾: al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Salawat are the churches." Likewise 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: They are the synagogues of the Jews, and they call them Salutha.

al-Suddi related, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that they are the churches of the Christians.

Abu al-'Aliyah and others said: The Salawat are the places of worship of the Sabians.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: The Salawat are mosques for the People of the Book and for the Muslims on the roads. As for the mosques, they are for the Muslims.

* *

His saying: ﴿In which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾. It has been said that the pronoun in ﴿in which it is mentioned﴾ refers to the mosques, since they are the nearest of what has been mentioned.

al-Dahhak said: All of them are places in which the name of Allah is much mentioned.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the monasteries of the monks, the churches of the Christians, and the synagogues of the Jews, which are their houses of worship, and the mosques of the Muslims in which the name of Allah is much mentioned, would all have been demolished, because this is the commonly used sense in the speech of the Arabs.

Some scholars said: This is an ascent from the lesser to the greater, until it reaches the mosques, which have the most who build them and the most who worship in them, and whose people have the sound intention.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ is like His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet. But those who disbelieve — for them is destruction, and He will waste their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 7–8].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty﴾: He described Himself with strength and might. By His strength He created everything and decreed it with precise decree. By His might, no subduer can overpower Him and no conqueror can defeat Him; rather, everything is humbled before Him and needy of Him. Whoever has the Strong, the Mighty as his helper is the one who is victorious, and his enemy is the one who is overpowered. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And already Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers — they will be the victorious.﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173]. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "Indeed I will prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 22, verses 42–46:

The Exalted says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of those among his people who opposed him: ﴿And if they deny you, then the people of Noah denied before them﴾ up to his saying [[In manuscripts F and A: "and ʿĀd and Thamud. And the people of Ibrahim and the people of Lut. And the companions of Madyan."]]: ﴿and Musa was denied﴾, meaning: despite what he brought of the clear signs and the manifest proofs.

﴿Then I gave the disbelievers respite﴾, meaning: I gave them time and delayed them. ﴿Then I seized them, and how was My disapproval?﴾, meaning: how was My rejection of them and My punishment of them?!

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) mentioned that the time between Pharaoh's saying to his people, ﴿I am your lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24], and God's destruction of him was forty years.

In the two Sahihs (the Sahih of al-Bukhari and the Sahih of Muslim) from Abu Musa, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then he recited: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4686), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2583).]].

Then He said: ﴿And how many a city did We destroy﴾, meaning: how many a city I have destroyed ﴿while it was wrongdoing﴾, meaning: denying its messenger. ﴿So it is fallen over its roofs﴾. Al-Dahhak said: its ceilings, meaning its dwellings have been ruined and its settlements abandoned.

﴿And a well left unused﴾, meaning: from which no one draws water, and no one comes to it after it was once frequented by many and crowded.

﴿And a palace elevated﴾. ʿIkrimah said: meaning one plastered with gypsum.

It is related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, Mujahid, ʿAta', Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Malih, and al-Dahhak, something similar to this.

Others said: it means high and raised.

Others said: strong, impregnable, and fortified.

All these sayings are close in meaning and there is no contradiction between them, for the solidity of its construction, its height, its firmness, and its fortification did not protect its people from the descent of God's might upon them, as He said: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers well-constructed﴾ [al-Nisa': 78].

* *

Harun ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us: Sayyar related to us: Ja'far related to us: Malik ibn Dinar said: God the Exalted revealed to Musa, peace be upon him: "O Musa, take for yourself two shoes of iron and a staff, then travel through the earth and seek out the traces and lessons, until the two shoes are worn through and the staff is broken."

He said: "No." Then he cited a verse of threat, and [Amr ibn 'Ubayd] said to him: "Are you a non-Arab? The Arabs consider going back on a promise to be baseness, and going back on a threat to be generosity. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:

"The son of my paternal uncle does not fear my wrath,
nor does the neighbour turn away from the might of one who threatens.
Indeed, if I threaten him or promise him,
I break my threat and fulfil my promise."

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾, that is, He, the Exalted, does not hasten. For a span of a thousand years in His creation is like one day with Him in relation to His judgement, because He knows that He is able to take retribution and that nothing escapes Him, even though He delays, gives respite, and allows [the wrongdoers] time. For this reason He said after this: ﴿And how many a town have I given respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman told me, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The poor among the Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, which is five hundred years."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] also narrated it from Abu Hurayrah as a mawquf report (attributed to a Companion, not the Prophet ﷺ), saying:

Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Sa'id al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Sumayr ibn Nahar, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: "The poor among the Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by the measure of half a day." I said: "And what is half a day?" He said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾.

[Editor's note: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2354; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11348. That is, half a day is five hundred years. Tafsir al-Tabari (17/129).]

Abu Dawud said at the end of the Book of Battles (Kitab al-Malahim) in his Sunan: 'Amr ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I truly hope that my Ummah will not fall short before its Lord, [in that] He will delay them by half a day." It was said to Sa'd: "And what is half a day?" He said: "Five hundred years."

[Editor's note: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4350.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾, that he said: "[It is] of the days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth."

It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Mahdi. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah also held this view, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal explicitly stated it in his book "al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyya" (Refutation of the Jahmiyya).

Mujahid said: This verse is like His saying: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Arim (Muhammad ibn al-Fadl) narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Atiq, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from a man from the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, who said: "Indeed Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, and ﴿indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾. He made the lifespan of this world six days, and He made the Hour on the seventh day. ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾. So the six days have passed, and you are on the seventh day. The likeness of this is that of a pregnant woman who has entered her final month: at whatever moment she gives birth, it is complete."

The Arabs consider going back on a promise to be baseness, and going back on a threat to be generosity. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:

"The son of my paternal uncle does not fear my wrath,
nor does the neighbour turn away from the might of one who threatens.
Indeed, if I threaten him or promise him,
I break my threat and fulfil my promise."

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾, that is, He, the Exalted, does not hasten. For a span of a thousand years in His creation is like one day with Him in relation to His judgement, because He knows that He is able to take retribution and that nothing escapes Him, even though He delays, gives respite, and allows [the wrongdoers] time. For this reason He said after this: ﴿And how many a town have I given respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman told me, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The poor among the Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, which is five hundred years."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] also narrated it from Abu Hurayrah as a mawquf report (attributed to a Companion, not the Prophet ﷺ), saying:

Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Sa'id al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Sumayr ibn Nahar, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: "The poor among the Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by the measure of half a day." I said: "And what is half a day?" He said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾.

[Editor's note: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2354; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11348. That is, half a day is five hundred years. Tafsir al-Tabari (17/129).]

Abu Dawud said at the end of the Book of Battles (Kitab al-Malahim) in his Sunan: 'Amr ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I truly hope that my Ummah will not fall short before its Lord, [in that] He will delay them by half a day." It was said to Sa'd: "And what is half a day?" He said: "Five hundred years."

[Editor's note: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4350.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾, that he said: "[It is] of the days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth."

It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Mahdi. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah also held this view, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal explicitly stated it in his book "al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyya" (Refutation of the Jahmiyya).

Mujahid said: This verse is like His saying: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Arim (Muhammad ibn al-Fadl) narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Atiq, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from a man from the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, who said: "Indeed Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, and ﴿indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾. He made the lifespan of this world six days, and He made the Hour on the seventh day. ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾. So the six days have passed, and you are on the seventh day. The likeness of this is that of a pregnant woman who has entered her final month: at whatever moment she gives birth, it is complete."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet ﷺ, when the disbelievers asked him to bring about the punishment and hastened it: ﴿Say: "O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you."﴾ That is, Allah has only sent me to you as a warner, before a severe punishment. "And I have no say over your reckoning; your affair is with Allah. If He wills, He hastens the punishment for you; if He wills, He delays it from you; if He wills, He accepts the repentance of whoever repents to Him; and if He wills, He misguides whoever He has decreed wretchedness for. He is the One who does what He wills, intends and chooses, [and] [[addition from F.]] ﴿There is no repeller of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 41]." And ﴿I am only a clear warner to you. So those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: that is, their hearts believe and they affirm their faith through their deeds, ﴿for them is forgiveness and an honorable provision﴾: that is, forgiveness for what has passed of their misdeeds, and a good recompense for the little of good they did.

[And] [[addition from T.]] Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "When you hear Allah the Exalted say ﴿and an honorable provision﴾, it is Paradise."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them﴾: Mujahid said: they discourage people from following the Prophet ﷺ. Likewise, 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr said: "discouraging" (muthabbitin).

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Mu'ajizin﴾ means "opposing" (muraghimin).

﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire﴾: it is the scorching fire, painful, its punishment and torment severe. May Allah protect us from it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah, We will increase them in punishment upon punishment because of what they used to spread corruption﴾ [An-Nahl: 88].

Many commentators (*mufassirun*, scholars of tafsir, or Qur'anic exegesis) have mentioned here the story of the Gharaniq (the "Cranes"), and the claim that many of the emigrants returned to the land of Abyssinia (al-Habasha) because they thought the polytheists of Quraysh had embraced Islam. However, all of its chains are *mursal* (disconnected, lacking a companion narrator), and I have not found it traced back through a sound, connected chain (*isnad*). And God knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited "al-Najm" (Surah 53) in Makkah, and when he reached this point: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾, [he said:] Satan threw upon his tongue: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for." They said: "He has never mentioned our gods with good before today." So he prostrated and they prostrated, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke, Satan cast [something] into his speech. But God abolishes what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm, and God is Knowing and Wise﴾ [[Addition from manuscript F and A: the words "the verse" appear in manuscript T.]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it, from Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, with its like. It is *mursal*. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from Yusuf ibn Hammad, from Umayyah ibn Khalid, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, as far as I think (the doubt is in the narration) that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited Surah "al-Najm" in Makkah until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza﴾, and he mentioned the rest. Then al-Bazzar said: It is not transmitted connected except through this chain; Umayyah ibn Khalid alone connected it, and he is a trustworthy and well-known narrator. This is only transmitted through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas [[In Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2263, "Kashf al-Astar."]].

Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu al-'Aliyah and from al-Suddi, as *mursal*. Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays, also as *mursal* [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/131).]].

Qatadah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was praying near the Maqam when he dozed off, and Satan cast upon his tongue: "Indeed their intercession is to be hoped for, and indeed they are among the exalted cranes," and the polytheists memorized it. Satan spread that the Prophet of God had recited it, and so their tongues slipped with it. Then God revealed: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke...﴾, the verse, and God repelled Satan.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Musa ibn Abi Musa al-Kufi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fulayh narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Ibn Shihab (al-Zuhri), who said: Surah "al-Najm" was revealed, and the polytheists used to say: "If this man mentioned our gods with good, we would acknowledge him and his companions. But he does not mention those who opposed his religion, the Jews and the Christians, with the kind of abuse and evil that he speaks of our gods." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was greatly distressed by what he and his companions suffered from their harm and denial, and their misguidance saddened him. So he longed for their guidance. When God revealed Surah "al-Najm," he recited: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is the male for you and the female for Him?﴾ Satan cast words at that point, when God mentioned the idols (*taghut*), and he said: "Indeed they are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is the one to be hoped for." This was from Satan's rhyming and his temptation. These two words fell into the heart of every polytheist in Makkah, their tongues slipped with them, and they rejoiced, saying: "Muhammad has returned to his former religion and the religion of his people." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reached the end of "al-Najm," he prostrated, and everyone present, Muslim or polytheist, prostrated with him. Except that al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah was an elderly man, so he raised a handful of dust and prostrated upon it. Both groups were amazed at their companions' prostration at the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) prostration. As for the Muslims, they were amazed at the polytheists prostrating with them without faith or certainty, for the Muslims had not heard the verse that Satan had cast into the polytheists' ears. Their souls were reassured by what Satan had cast into the wish of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and Satan told them that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had recited it in the surah, so they prostrated to glorify their gods. That statement spread among the people, and Satan publicized it, until it reached the land of Abyssinia and the Muslims there, including 'Uthman ibn Maz'un and his companions. They related that the people of Makkah had all embraced Islam and prayed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). It reached them that al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah had prostrated on the dust with his hand. They were told that the Muslims were safe in Makkah, so they came back quickly. But God had abrogated what Satan had cast, made His verses firm, and protected him (the Prophet) from fabrication. God said: ﴿We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke, Satan cast [something] into his speech. Then God abolishes what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm, and God is Knowing and Wise. * That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened, and indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾. When God made clear His decree and cleared him of Satan's rhyming, the polytheists returned to their misguidance and their enmity toward the Muslims, and they grew harsher against them. This too is *mursal*.

In the tafsir of Ibn Jarir, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, there is something similar [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/133).]]. The imam Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in his book *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah* (Proofs of Prophethood), but he did not trace it back to Musa ibn 'Uqbah; he related it in his *Maghazi* (military expeditions) in similar form, and he said: "We have also transmitted this story from Ibn Ishaq."

I say: Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned it in the *Sirah* in something close to this, and all of these are *mursalat* and *munqati'at* (broken chains). And God knows best. Al-Baghawi also cited it in his tafsir, collecting it from the statements of Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others, in similar form. Then he raised a question here: how could such a thing happen given the guaranteed protection (*'ismah*) that God granted His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him? He then recorded various answers from people, among the most subtle of which is that Satan put that into the ears of the polytheists, so they imagined it came from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when in reality it was not so, but was rather Satan's doing and not from the Messenger of the Merciful (ﷺ). And God knows best [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (5/394).]].

Thus the answers of the theologians (*mutakallimun*) on this matter have varied, assuming its authenticity. Qadi 'Iyad, may God have mercy on him, addressed this in his book *al-Shifa*, and answered with what amounts to the following [[This is what appears in all manuscripts. The words of Qadi 'Iyad in *al-Shifa* (2/107) I quote in summary. He said, may God honor you:

"Know that we have two approaches in discussing the problematic nature of this hadith: one is to weaken its basis, and the other is to accept it hypothetically.

As for the first approach: it is enough for you that this is a hadith that none of the people of authentic transmission has recorded, nor has any trustworthy narrator transmitted it with a sound, connected chain. Rather, it is the exegetes and historians, who are infatuated with everything strange and who snatch from the pages every sound and every weak report, who have become attached to it and its like.

The judge Bakr ibn al-'Ala al-Maliki spoke truly when he said: People have been afflicted with some of the people of desires and of tafsir, and heretics have clung to this, despite the weakness of its transmitters, the disorder of its narrations, the disconnection of its chain, and the variation of its wording. One says it occurred during prayer; another says he said it in his people's assembly when the surah was revealed; another says he said it when afflicted by drowsiness; another says he merely spoke in his heart and erred; another says Satan said it upon his tongue, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) presented it to Gabriel, he said: 'That is not how I taught you'; and another says that Satan informed them that the Prophet (ﷺ) had recited it, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) heard of this he said: 'By God, it was not revealed like this.'

And there are other differences among the narrators. As for those among the exegetes and the Successors (*tabi'un*) from whom this account is related, none of them traced it to a companion, nor did they raise it to a Companion, and most of the chains from them on this are weak and flimsy.

As for the *marfu'* (traced to the Prophet) report in it, it is the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said, as I think (the doubt is in the hadith), that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and he mentioned the story.

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: We do not know this to be transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) through a connected chain that can be cited except this one, and only Umayyah ibn Khalid connected it from Shu'bah; others transmit it as *mursal* from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and it is known only through al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

So Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, has shown you that it is not known through any route that may be cited other than this, and in it there is weakness that he pointed out, together with the doubt in it, as we have mentioned, which means it cannot be relied upon, and there is no certainty with it.

As for the hadith of al-Kalbi, it is not permissible to narrate it or mention it because of its extreme weakness and fabrication, as al-Bazzar, may God have mercy on him, indicated.

What is authentic (*sahih*) in this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "al-Najm" while in Makkah, and the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and mankind prostrated with him. This is its refutation from the standpoint of transmission.

As for the meaning: the proof has been established, and the community has agreed upon his infallibility (*'ismah*), and his freedom from such vileness, either by his wishing that something like this, praising gods other than God, would be revealed to him, which is disbelief, or by Satan climbing up to him and confusing the Qur'an so that he adds to it what is not part of it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) believes that some of the Qur'an is not from it, until Gabriel (peace be upon him) alerts him. All of that is impossible in his case (ﷺ).

Or the Prophet (ﷺ) would say that from himself deliberately, which is disbelief, or by mistake, and he is protected from all of that.

The second point is the impossibility of this story by reason and custom: for if this speech were as it is reported, it would be poorly joined, self-contradictory in its parts, mixing praise with blame, and its composition and arrangement would be broken. And the Prophet (ﷺ), and those present with him among the Muslims and the chiefs of the polytheists, could not have failed to notice this.

This is not hidden from the least careful reflection, so how about one whose intellect is weighty and whose knowledge of eloquent speech and its expression is vast!?

The third point: it is known from the habit of the hypocrites, the stubborn polytheists, the weak-hearted, and the ignorant among the Muslims, that they recoil at the first appearance of a thing, and that the enemy confuses the Prophet (ﷺ) at the slightest trial, that they reproach the Muslims and gloat over them from time to time, and that whoever has disease in his heart and has professed Islam apostatizes at the slightest doubt...

No one has related anything in this story except this weak report.

The fourth point: the narrators of this matter mention that the verses ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from what We revealed to you...﴾ (17:73–74) were revealed concerning it. These two verses refute the report they transmitted, for God mentioned that they almost tempted him so that he would fabricate against Him, and that had He not made him firm, he would have nearly inclined toward them.

The meaning and implication of this is that God protected him from fabricating, and made him firm so that he did not incline toward them even slightly, let alone greatly. Yet they narrate in their weak reports that he went beyond inclining and fabricating, by praising their gods, and that he said (ﷺ): 'You have fabricated against God and said what He did not say.' This is the opposite of the implication of the verse, and the verse weakens the hadith even if it were sound, so how much more so when it is not sound at all. This is like His words in another verse: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all﴾ (4:113).

As for the second approach: it is based on accepting the hadith, if it were sound. God has kept us from its soundness, but in any case the imams of the Muslims have answered this with various answers, some weak and some strong.

Then he mentioned the answers to that (2/111–114). Among those who rejected them was Imam Ibn Khuzaymah, who said: 'This is from the fabrication of the heretics (*zanadiqah*),' and this is the correct position."

For further reading: see *al-Isra'iliyyat wa al-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir* (p. 314) by Muhammad Abu Shahbah, and *Nasb al-Majaniq li-Ibtal Qissat al-Gharaniq* by Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿except that when he spoke, Satan cast [something] into his speech﴾. This is a consolation to him, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him; that is, let that not disturb you, for such a thing happened to those messengers and prophets before you.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿into his wish﴾ means: when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, and God nullifies what Satan casts, and God makes His verses firm.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verses 52–54 (part 2 of 2):

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿When he desires [Satan casts into his desire]﴾, meaning: when he speaks, Satan casts into his speech.

Mujahid said: ﴿When he desires﴾ [the addition is from the manuscripts F and A], meaning: when he says.

It is also said that ﴿his desire﴾ means his recitation, as in ﴿but only wishful fancies﴾ [al-Baqarah: 78], that is, they recite but do not write.

Al-Baghawi said: Most of the exegetes said that the meaning of His words ﴿desires﴾ is: he recited and read the Book of Allah. ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ means: into his recitation. The poet said about 'Uthman when he was killed:

He desired the Book of Allah at the first of the night,
and at its end he met the doom of the fates.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿When he desires﴾ means: when he recites.

Ibn Jarir said: This statement is closer to the true interpretation of the speech.

* *

As for His words ﴿then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾: the linguistic reality of naskh (abrogation, i.e. removal) is removal and lifting.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: That is, Allah, glorified and exalted, nullifies what Satan cast.

Al-Dahhak said: Jibril abrogated by the command of Allah what Satan cast, and Allah made His verses firm.

* *

As for His words ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing [Knowing, Wise, in some manuscripts]﴾, meaning: of what occurs of matters and events, nothing hidden is concealed from Him; ﴿All-Wise﴾, meaning: in His decree, His creation and His command. To Him belong perfect wisdom and conclusive proof. Therefore He said: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning: doubt, polytheism, disbelief and hypocrisy, like the polytheists when they rejoiced at that and believed it to be true, though it was from Satan.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ are the hypocrites, and ﴿those whose hearts are hardened﴾ are the polytheists.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They are the Jews.

﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme schism﴾, meaning: in misguidance, opposition and far-reaching obstinacy from the truth and rightness.

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it﴾, meaning: and that those who have been given beneficial knowledge, by which they distinguish truth from falsehood, the believers in Allah and His Messenger, may know that what We have revealed to you is the truth from your Lord, which He sent down with His knowledge and His preservation, and guarded against anything else mixing with it. Rather, it is a Wise Book: ﴿falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42].

* *

As for His words ﴿so that they believe in it﴾, meaning: that they confirm it and submit to it. ﴿And their hearts humble themselves to Him﴾, meaning: they become submissive and lowly. ﴿And indeed Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. In this world He guides them to the truth and following it, and grants them success in opposing falsehood and avoiding it; and in the Hereafter He guides them [to] [the addition is from manuscript A] the straight path, which leads to the ranks of the Gardens, and keeps them away from the painful punishment and the lowest levels of the Fire.

These two words fell into the heart of every polytheist in Makkah, their tongues slipped with them, and they rejoiced, saying: "Muhammad has returned to his former religion and the religion of his people." "Know that we have two approaches in discussing the problematic nature of this hadith: one is to weaken its basis, and the other is to accept it hypothetically.

All of that is impossible in his case (ﷺ).

Or the Prophet (ﷺ) would say that from himself deliberately, which is disbelief, or by mistake, and he is protected from all of that.

The second point is the impossibility of this story by reason and custom: for if this speech were as it is reported, it would be poorly joined, self-contradictory in its parts, mixing praise with blame, and its composition and arrangement would be broken. And the Prophet (ﷺ), and those present with him among the Muslims and the chiefs of the polytheists, could not have failed to notice this.

This is not hidden from the least careful reflection, so how about one whose intellect is weighty and whose knowledge of eloquent speech and its expression is vast!?

The third point: it is known from the habit of the hypocrites, the stubborn polytheists, the weak-hearted, and the ignorant among the Muslims, that they recoil at the first appearance of a thing, and that the enemy confuses the Prophet (ﷺ) at the slightest trial, that they reproach the Muslims and gloat over them from time to time, and that whoever has disease in his heart and has professed Islam apostatizes at the slightest doubt...

No one has related anything in this story except this weak report.

This is the opposite of the implication of the verse, and the verse weakens the hadith even if it were sound, so how much more so when it is not sound at all. As for the second approach: it is based on accepting the hadith, if it were sound. God has kept us from its soundness, but in any case the imams of the Muslims have answered this with various answers, some weak and some strong.

Then he mentioned the answers to that (2/111–114). Among those who rejected them was Imam Ibn Khuzaymah, who said: 'This is from the fabrication of the heretics (*zanadiqah*),' and this is the correct position."

So Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, has shown you that it is not known through any route that may be cited other than this, and in it there is weakness that he pointed out, together with the doubt in it, as we have mentioned, which means it cannot be relied upon, and there is no certainty with it.

As for the hadith of al-Kalbi, it is not permissible to narrate it or mention it because of its extreme weakness and fabrication, as al-Bazzar, may God have mercy on him, indicated.

What is authentic (*sahih*) in this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "al-Najm" while in Makkah, and the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and mankind prostrated with him. This is its refutation from the standpoint of transmission.

As for the meaning: the proof has been established, and the community has agreed upon his infallibility (*'ismah*), and his freedom from such vileness, either by his wishing that something like this, praising gods other than God, would be revealed to him, which is disbelief, or by Satan climbing up to him and confusing the Qur'an so that he adds to it what is not part of it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) believes that some of the Qur'an is not from it, until Gabriel (peace be upon him) alerts him. All of that is impossible in his case (ﷺ).

Or the Prophet (ﷺ) would say that from himself deliberately, which is disbelief, or by mistake, and he is protected from all of that.

The second point is the impossibility of this story by reason and custom: for if this speech were as it is reported, it would be poorly joined, self-contradictory in its parts, mixing praise with blame, and its composition and arrangement would be broken. And the Prophet (ﷺ), and those present with him among the Muslims and the chiefs of the polytheists, could not have failed to notice this.

This is not hidden from the least careful reflection, so how about one whose intellect is weighty and whose knowledge of eloquent speech and its expression is vast!?

The third point: it is known from the habit of the hypocrites, the stubborn polytheists, the weak-hearted, and the ignorant among the Muslims, that they recoil at the first appearance of a thing, and that the enemy confuses the Prophet (ﷺ) at the slightest trial, that they reproach the Muslims and gloat over them from time to time, and that whoever has disease in his heart and has professed Islam apostatizes at the slightest doubt...

No one has related anything in this story except this weak report.

The fourth point: the narrators of this matter mention that the verses ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from what We revealed to you...﴾ (17:73–74) were revealed concerning it. These two verses refute the report they transmitted, for God mentioned that they almost tempted him so that he would fabricate against Him, and that had He not made him firm, he would have nearly inclined toward them.

The meaning and implication of this is that God protected him from fabricating, and made him firm so that he did not incline toward them even slightly, let alone greatly. Yet they narrate in their weak reports that he went beyond inclining and fabricating, by praising their gods, and that he said (ﷺ): 'You have fabricated against God and said what He did not say.' This is the opposite of the implication of the verse, and the verse weakens the hadith even if it were sound, so how much more so when it is not sound at all. This is like His words in another verse: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all﴾ (4:113).

As for the second approach: it is based on accepting the hadith, if it were sound. God has kept us from its soundness, but in any case the imams of the Muslims have answered this with various answers, some weak and some strong.

Then he mentioned the answers to that (2/111–114). Among those who rejected them was Imam Ibn Khuzaymah, who said: 'This is from the fabrication of the heretics (*zanadiqah*),' and this is the correct position."
