As for His words: ﴿except that when he spoke, Satan cast [something] into his speech﴾. This is a consolation to him, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him; that is, let that not disturb you, for such a thing happened to those messengers and prophets before you.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿into his wish﴾ means: when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, and God nullifies what Satan casts, and God makes His verses firm.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 22, verses 52–54 (part 2 of 2):

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿When he desires [Satan casts into his desire]﴾, meaning: when he speaks, Satan casts into his speech.

Mujahid said: ﴿When he desires﴾ [the addition is from the manuscripts F and A], meaning: when he says.

It is also said that ﴿his desire﴾ means his recitation, as in ﴿but only wishful fancies﴾ [al-Baqarah: 78], that is, they recite but do not write.

Al-Baghawi said: Most of the exegetes said that the meaning of His words ﴿desires﴾ is: he recited and read the Book of Allah. ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ means: into his recitation. The poet said about 'Uthman when he was killed:

He desired the Book of Allah at the first of the night,
and at its end he met the doom of the fates.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿When he desires﴾ means: when he recites.

Ibn Jarir said: This statement is closer to the true interpretation of the speech.

* *

As for His words ﴿then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾: the linguistic reality of naskh (abrogation, i.e. removal) is removal and lifting.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: That is, Allah, glorified and exalted, nullifies what Satan cast.

Al-Dahhak said: Jibril abrogated by the command of Allah what Satan cast, and Allah made His verses firm.

* *

As for His words ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing [Knowing, Wise, in some manuscripts]﴾, meaning: of what occurs of matters and events, nothing hidden is concealed from Him; ﴿All-Wise﴾, meaning: in His decree, His creation and His command. To Him belong perfect wisdom and conclusive proof. Therefore He said: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning: doubt, polytheism, disbelief and hypocrisy, like the polytheists when they rejoiced at that and believed it to be true, though it was from Satan.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ are the hypocrites, and ﴿those whose hearts are hardened﴾ are the polytheists.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They are the Jews.

﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme schism﴾, meaning: in misguidance, opposition and far-reaching obstinacy from the truth and rightness.

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it﴾, meaning: and that those who have been given beneficial knowledge, by which they distinguish truth from falsehood, the believers in Allah and His Messenger, may know that what We have revealed to you is the truth from your Lord, which He sent down with His knowledge and His preservation, and guarded against anything else mixing with it. Rather, it is a Wise Book: ﴿falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42].

* *

As for His words ﴿so that they believe in it﴾, meaning: that they confirm it and submit to it. ﴿And their hearts humble themselves to Him﴾, meaning: they become submissive and lowly. ﴿And indeed Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. In this world He guides them to the truth and following it, and grants them success in opposing falsehood and avoiding it; and in the Hereafter He guides them [to] [the addition is from manuscript A] the straight path, which leads to the ranks of the Gardens, and keeps them away from the painful punishment and the lowest levels of the Fire.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, reporting about the disbelievers: they will not cease to be in doubt (miryah) about this Qur'an, meaning in uncertainty and suspicion. This was said by Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿minhu﴾ ("of it") means "of what Satan cast."

﴿Until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾: Mujahid said, "unexpectedly." Qatada said: ﴿baghtatan﴾ (suddenly), the command of Allah overtook the people suddenly. Allah never seized a people except at the height of their intoxication (sakra), their delusion (gharra) and their comfort (ni'mah). So do not be deceived by Allah, for none is deceived by Allah except the defiantly disobedient people (al-qawm al-fasiqun).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day﴾: Mujahid said, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, it is the Day of Badr. Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and others besides them said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Ikrimah and Mujahid (in one narration from them both) said: it is the Day of Resurrection, which has no night. Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri also said this.

This second view is the correct one. Although the Day of Badr was among the things they were threatened with, this is what is meant; hence He said: ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them﴾, like His saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], and His saying: ﴿The dominion on that Day will be true for the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Furqan: 26].

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: their hearts believed, they affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acted in accordance with what they knew, and their hearts, their words and their deeds were in harmony.

﴿They will be in Gardens of Bliss﴾: meaning they will have enduring bliss, which does not change, does not pass away, and does not perish.

﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾, meaning: their hearts disbelieved in the truth, they rejected it and denied it, opposed the Messengers, and were arrogant toward following them; ﴿for them is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning: a recompense for their arrogance and their turning away from the truth and their refusal, like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: abased.

He informs us about those who emigrated (hijrah, migration) in the cause of God, seeking His good pleasure and desiring what is with Him. They left their homelands, their families and their friends, and departed from their lands for the sake of God and His Messenger, in support of the religion of God. ﴿Then they were killed﴾, that is, in jihad, ﴿or they died﴾, that is, by natural death, dying in their beds without fighting. They have attained a great reward and a fine commendation, as God the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to God and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed become due from God﴾ [An-Nisa: 100].

* *

His saying: ﴿God will certainly provide for them a goodly provision﴾, that is, He will bestow upon them from His bounty and provision in Paradise that which will delight their eyes. ﴿Indeed, God is surely the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with﴾, that is, Paradise. As God the Exalted says: ﴿But if he is among those brought near [to God], then rest and provision and a Garden of Pleasure﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 88-89]. So He informs that such a person will obtain rest, provision, and the Garden of Pleasure, just as He says here: ﴿God will certainly provide for them a goodly provision﴾. Then He said: ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, God is Knowing, Forbearing﴾, that is, Knowing of those who emigrate and strive in His way, and of who deserves that [reward]. ﴿Forbearing﴾, that is, He is forbearing, overlooks, and forgives them their sins, and expiates them for them through their emigration to Him and their reliance upon Him. As for those who are killed in the way of God, whether they were emigrants or not, they are alive with their Lord and are provided for, as God the Exalted says: ﴿And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169]. The narrations on this are numerous, as has previously been mentioned. As for those who die in the way of God, whether they were emigrants or not, this noble verse together with the authentic hadiths includes the continuation of provision for them and the great kindness of God toward them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, from Ibn al-Harith, meaning 'Abd al-Karim, from Ibn 'Uqbah, meaning Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Uqbah, who said: Shurahbil ibn al-Simt narrated to us: Our garrison duty (ribat) and our stay at a fortress in the land of the Romans were prolonged. Then Salman, meaning al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by me and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever dies while on garrison duty, Allah will continue for him the like of that reward, will continue provision for him, and he will be secure from the tempters (al-fattanin).'" And recite, if you wish: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died - God will surely provide for them a goodly provision. And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, God is Knowing and Forbearing﴾.

He also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Zayd ibn Bishr narrated to us, Hammam informed me that he heard Abu Qubayl and Rabi'ah ibn Sayf al-Mu'afiri say: "We were at Rhodes, and with us was Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd al-Ansari, a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He passed by two funerals, one of a slain man and the other of one who had died naturally. The people inclined toward the slain man. Fadalah said: 'Why do I see the people inclining toward this one and leaving this one?' They said: 'This is one slain in the way of God, the Exalted.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised. Listen to the Book of God: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died [God will surely provide for them a goodly provision, and indeed, God is the best of providers]﴾ [[Addition from F; in H and T: "up to the end of the verse."]].'"

He also said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, Sallaman ibn 'Amir al-Sha'bani narrated to us, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jahdam al-Khawlani narrated to him that he was present with Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd at sea with two funerals, one of whom had been struck by a catapult (manjaniq) and the other had died. Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd sat by the grave of the one who had died. It was said to him: "You left the martyr and did not sit by him?" He said: "I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised. Indeed, Allah says: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died [God will surely provide for them a goodly provision. And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance] [[Addition from F; in T: "up to his saying."]] that they will be pleased with﴾. So what would you desire, O servant, when you are admitted to an entrance you are pleased with and are granted a goodly provision? By Allah, I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Ala, from Ibn Wahb, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh informed me, from Sallaman ibn 'Amir, who said: Fadalah was at Rhodes as commander over the quarters (al-arba'), and he went out with the funerals of two men, one of whom had been slain and the other had died... He then mentioned something similar to what has preceded [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/136).]].

So the Muslims fought them, and God gave them victory over them, [and] [[Addition from A.]] ﴿Indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾.

He informs us about those who emigrated (hijrah, migration) in the cause of God, seeking His good pleasure and desiring what is with Him. They left their homelands, their families and their friends, and departed from their lands for the sake of God and His Messenger, in support of the religion of God. ﴿Then they were killed﴾, that is, in jihad, ﴿or they died﴾, that is, by natural death, dying in their beds without fighting. They have attained a great reward and a fine commendation, as God the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to God and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed become due from God﴾ [An-Nisa: 100].

* *

His saying: ﴿God will certainly provide for them a goodly provision﴾, that is, He will bestow upon them from His bounty and provision in Paradise that which will delight their eyes. ﴿Indeed, God is surely the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with﴾, that is, Paradise. As God the Exalted says: ﴿But if he is among those brought near [to God], then rest and provision and a Garden of Pleasure﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 88-89]. So He informs that such a person will obtain rest, provision, and the Garden of Pleasure, just as He says here: ﴿God will certainly provide for them a goodly provision﴾. Then He said: ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, God is Knowing, Forbearing﴾, that is, Knowing of those who emigrate and strive in His way, and of who deserves that [reward]. ﴿Forbearing﴾, that is, He is forbearing, overlooks, and forgives them their sins, and expiates them for them through their emigration to Him and their reliance upon Him. As for those who are killed in the way of God, whether they were emigrants or not, they are alive with their Lord and are provided for, as God the Exalted says: ﴿And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169]. The narrations on this are numerous, as has previously been mentioned. As for those who die in the way of God, whether they were emigrants or not, this noble verse together with the authentic hadiths includes the continuation of provision for them and the great kindness of God toward them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, from Ibn al-Harith, meaning 'Abd al-Karim, from Ibn 'Uqbah, meaning Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Uqbah, who said: Shurahbil ibn al-Simt narrated to us: Our garrison duty (ribat) and our stay at a fortress in the land of the Romans were prolonged. Then Salman, meaning al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by me and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever dies while on garrison duty, Allah will continue for him the like of that reward, will continue provision for him, and he will be secure from the tempters (al-fattanin).'" And recite, if you wish: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died - God will surely provide for them a goodly provision. And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, God is Knowing and Forbearing﴾.

He also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Zayd ibn Bishr narrated to us, Hammam informed me that he heard Abu Qubayl and Rabi'ah ibn Sayf al-Mu'afiri say: "We were at Rhodes, and with us was Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd al-Ansari, a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He passed by two funerals, one of a slain man and the other of one who had died naturally. The people inclined toward the slain man. Fadalah said: 'Why do I see the people inclining toward this one and leaving this one?' They said: 'This is one slain in the way of God, the Exalted.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised. Listen to the Book of God: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died [God will surely provide for them a goodly provision, and indeed, God is the best of providers]﴾ [[Addition from F; in H and T: "up to the end of the verse."]].'"

He also said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, Sallaman ibn 'Amir al-Sha'bani narrated to us, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jahdam al-Khawlani narrated to him that he was present with Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd at sea with two funerals, one of whom had been struck by a catapult (manjaniq) and the other had died. Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd sat by the grave of the one who had died. It was said to him: "You left the martyr and did not sit by him?" He said: "I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised. Indeed, Allah says: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of God and then were killed or died [God will surely provide for them a goodly provision. And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance] [[Addition from F; in T: "up to his saying."]] that they will be pleased with﴾. So what would you desire, O servant, when you are admitted to an entrance you are pleased with and are granted a goodly provision? By Allah, I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Ala, from Ibn Wahb, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh informed me, from Sallaman ibn 'Amir, who said: Fadalah was at Rhodes as commander over the quarters (al-arba'), and he went out with the funerals of two men, one of whom had been slain and the other had died... He then mentioned something similar to what has preceded [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/136).]].

Allah, exalted is He, says, drawing attention to the fact that He is the Creator who disposes of His creation as He wills, as He said: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You endow with honor whom You will and You bring low whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent. You cause the night to enter the day and You cause the day to enter the night. And You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living. And You give provision to whom You will without account."﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 26, 27]. The meaning of His causing the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night is that He inserts each into the other: at times He lengthens the night and shortens the day, as in winter, and at times He lengthens the day and shortens the night, as in summer.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ means: He hears the statements of His servants and sees them, nothing of them is hidden from Him in their conditions, their movements and their stillness.

When He had explained that He is the one who disposes of existence, the Judge whose judgment none can repel, He said: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾, meaning: the true God, to whom alone worship is due, because He is the possessor of great dominion, whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be, and everything is in need of Him and humbled before Him. ﴿And that what they invoke other than Him is falsehood﴾, meaning: [the idols], the rivals and the images. Everything that is worshipped besides Allah, exalted is He, is false, because it does not possess harm or benefit.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is the Most High, the Grand﴾, as He said: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Great﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255], and He said: ﴿the Grand, the Exalted﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 9]. So everything is under His subjugation, authority and greatness; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him, because He is the Great than whom there is none greater, the Most High than whom there is none higher, the Grand than whom there is none grander. Exalted, sanctified and glorified is He, mighty and majestic, above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation.

His saying ﴿so the earth becomes green﴾: the fa' here indicates sequence (ta'qib), and the sequence of each thing follows its own nature, as He said: ﴿We created the drop into a clinging clot, then We created the clot into a lump, then We created the lump into bones﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. "Say to Him: Who causes the seed to grow in the soil,

And He brings forth from it its grain in its heads.
In that are signs for whoever has understanding."

"Say to Him: Who causes the seed to grow in the soil,
so that from it the herb becomes swaying and rising?
And He brings forth from it its grain in its heads.
In that are signs for whoever has understanding."

[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham (1/228).]

* *

His saying ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ means: all things belong to His dominion. He is free of need from anything other than Himself, and everything is in need of Him, a servant before Him.

* *

His saying ﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth﴾ means: of animals, inanimate things, crops, and fruits. As He said: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], meaning: by His kindness, bounty, and favor. ﴿And the ship runs upon the sea by His command﴾ means: by His subjection and His directing. That is, in the turbulent sea and the clashing of waves, the ship runs with its people by a good wind, with gentleness and deliberation. They carry in it whatever they wish of merchandise, goods, and benefits from one land to another and from one region to another. They bring what is with those people to these, just as they take what is with these to those, of what they need, seek, and desire. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission﴾ means: if He willed, He would permit the sky to fall upon the earth, and whoever is on it would perish. But by His gentleness, mercy, and power, He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward mankind﴾, meaning: despite their wrongdoing, as He said in another verse: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is Forgiving to the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6].

* *

His saying ﴿And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then will give you life. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ is like His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He brought you to life? Then He will cause you to die, then bring you to life, then to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. It is also like His saying: ﴿Say: Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 26], and His saying: ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice﴾ [Ghafir: 11].

The meaning of the statement is: How do you make rivals (andad) with Allah and worship others besides Him, when He alone is independent in creation, provision, and disposal? ﴿And it is He who gave you life﴾ means: He created you after you were not a thing worthy of mention, and brought you into existence. ﴿Then causes you to die, then gives you life﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ means: deniers and ingrates.

Allah informs that He has made for every community a rite (manasik).

Ibn Jarir said: That is, for every nation of a prophet, a rite. He said: The root of manasik in the speech of the Arabs is the place that a person frequents and returns to, whether for good or for evil. He said: For this reason the rites of the Hajj (manasik al-Hajj) were named thus, because people return to them repeatedly and cling to them.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/138).]

If the meaning is as he said, that the intended sense is "For every community We have made a rite," then the meaning of His words ﴿So let them not dispute with you about the matter﴾ is: these polytheists. But if the meaning is: "For every community We have made a rite" by a decree of predestination (ja'lan qadariyyan), as He said: ﴿And for each there is a direction toward which it turns﴾ [al-Baqarah: 148], and for this reason He said here: ﴿they are performing it﴾, that is, doing it, then the pronoun here refers to those who have rites and ways. That is: these people only do this by the decree and will of Allah, so do not be affected by their disputing with you, and let that not divert you from the truth you are upon. For this reason He said: ﴿And invite to your Lord; indeed, you are upon a straight guidance﴾, that is, a clear, straight path that leads to the goal.

This is like His saying: ﴿And let them not hinder you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you, and invite to your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 87].

And His saying: ﴿And if they argue with you, say, "Allah is most knowing of what you do"﴾, like His saying: ﴿And if they deny you, say, "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do"﴾ [Yunus: 41].

* *

And His saying: ﴿Allah is most knowing of what you do﴾ is a severe warning and an emphatic threat, like His saying: ﴿He is most knowing of what you spread forth concerning it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8]. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which you used to differ﴾.

This is like His saying: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say, "I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture, and I have been commanded to act justly among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return"﴾ [al-Shura: 15].

He, exalted is He, informs us of the perfection of His knowledge of His creation, and that He encompasses what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. Not even the weight of an atom's particle escapes Him, whether in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater. He, exalted is He, knew all created things before their existence, and recorded that in His Book, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), as established in Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah decreed the destinies of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was upon the water." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2653), with the wording "Allah wrote the destinies of the creatures."]]

In the Sunan (the collections of hadith), from the narrations of a group of the Companions, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing that Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'And what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what is to be, until the Day of Resurrection.' So the pen ran with what is to be until the Day of Resurrection." [[It comes from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit: narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (4700), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3319), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." It also comes from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (p. 378).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, Ata ibn Dinar narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "Allah created the Preserved Tablet, the distance of a hundred years' travel. And before He created the creation, He said to the pen, while it was upon the Throne, blessed and exalted is He: 'Write.' The pen said: 'And what shall I write?' He said: 'My knowledge concerning My creation until the Hour is established.' So the pen ran with what is to be in the knowledge of Allah until the Day of Resurrection." This is the meaning of His saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Did you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth?﴾

This is part of the completeness of His knowledge, exalted is He, that He knew things before they came into being, and also decreed and recorded them. So whatever the servants do, He knew it before that, in the manner in which they will do it. He knows before the creation that this one will obey by his own choice, and that one will disobey by his own choice, and He recorded that with Him, and He encompasses everything in knowledge. That is easy for Him and effortless for Him. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed that is in a Book. Indeed that is easy for Allah.﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, in his commentary on Surah al-Hajj, verses 71–72:

He, exalted is He, says, informing about the polytheists in what they ignored and disbelieved, and worshipped besides Allah that for which He had sent down no authority (sultan), meaning: no proof or evidence, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever calls upon another god along with Allah, for which he has no proof – then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 117]. And therefore He said here: ﴿for which He has sent down no authority, and about which they have no knowledge﴾, i.e., they have no knowledge concerning what they have invented and fabricated, and it is only a matter they received from their forefathers and ancestors, without any evidence or proof. Its origin is from what Satan embellished for them and adorned for them. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, threatened them with His saying: ﴿And for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾, i.e., no helper who would help them against Allah in what punishment and retribution will befall them.

Then He said: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences﴾, i.e., when the verses of the Qur'an, and the proofs and clear evidences of Allah's oneness, that there is no god except Him, and that His noble messengers are true and truthful, are mentioned to them, ﴿you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve a denial (of the truth)﴾... They almost attack those who recite Our verses to them, i.e., they almost rush at those who argue against them with the sound proofs of the Qur'an, and they stretch out their hands and tongues against them with evil! ﴿Say﴾, i.e., O Muhammad, to these people: ﴿Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve.﴾ [[In T, F, A: "disbelieve and wretched is the destination."]] i.e., the Fire, its punishment and its retribution are more severe, more difficult, more overwhelming and greater than what you threaten the friends of Allah, the believers, with in this world; and the punishment of the Hereafter for your conduct is greater than what you inflict upon them, if you inflict it by your claim and your intention.

* *

His saying: ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., wretched is the Fire as an abode, a resting place, a place of return, a refuge and a dwelling, ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and a station﴾ [Al-Furqan: 66].

"O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it." Meaning: for what the ignorant ones who associate partners with Allah worship. "So listen to it" means: be silent and understand. "Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah" means: even if all the idols and rivals you worship gathered together to create a single fly, they would not be able to do so.

Imam Ahmad said:

Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'a, from Abu Hurayra, who raised the hadith, that he said: "And who is more unjust than one who creates [a creation] [[Addition from manuscripts T and F, and al-Musnad.]] like My creation? Let them create the like of My creation: an atom, or a fly, or a grain." [[al-Musnad (2/391).]]

The two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it through the chain of Umarah, from Abu Zur'a, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And who is more unjust than one who sets out to create like My creation? Let them create an atom; let them create a barleycorn." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5953), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2111).]]

Then Allah, the Exalted, also said: "And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not retrieve it from it." Meaning: they are powerless to create a single fly. Moreover, and more emphatically, they are powerless to resist it and to take revenge on it. If it snatched from them something of the perfume that is on them, and then they wanted to retrieve it from it, they would not be able to do so. This is despite the fact that the fly is among the weakest and most insignificant of Allah's creatures. For this reason He said: "Weak are the seeker and the sought."

Ibn Abbas said: "The seeker" is the idol, and "the sought" is the fly. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view, and it is the apparent sense of the context. Al-Suddi and others said: "The seeker" is the worshipper, and "the sought" is the idol.

Then He said: "They did not esteem Allah with His true esteem." Meaning: they did not know the greatness and majesty of Allah when they worshipped others alongside Him, [others] such as this one, which cannot resist a fly because of its weakness and helplessness. "Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty." Meaning: He is the Strong, who by His power and might created everything. "It is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him" [al-Rum: 27]. "Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats" [al-Buruj: 12–13]. "Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm" [al-Dhariyat: 58].

* *

His saying "Mighty" (Aziz) means: He has overcome everything, subdued it and prevailed over it, so none can resist Him or contend with Him, due to His greatness and sovereignty. He is the One, the Subduer.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs that He chooses messengers from among the angels, according to what He wills of His legislation and decree, and from among mankind to convey His messages. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, meaning: He hears the words of His servants, sees them, and knows who among them deserves this (honour), as He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

* *

His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah are all matters returned﴾ means: He knows what they do with His messengers in what He has sent them with, so nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, as He said: ﴿[He is] the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved. Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards, that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompasses what is with them, and He has enumerated everything in number﴾ [al-Jinn: 26-28]. So He, glorified is He, is Watchful over them, Witness to what is said to them, Protector of them, and Supporter of their cause. ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], and the verse continues.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs that He chooses messengers from among the angels, according to what He wills of His legislation and decree, and from among mankind to convey His messages. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, meaning: He hears the words of His servants, sees them, and knows who among them deserves this (honour), as He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed over this second prostration in Surah al-Hajj, whether prostration is prescribed in it or not, and there are two opinions. Earlier, at the first prostration, we mentioned the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Surah al-Hajj has been given two prostrations, so whoever does not prostrate for them should not recite them."

* *

Allah's words: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾, meaning with your wealth, your tongues, and your selves, as He said: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102].

* *

Allah's words: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, meaning: O this Ummah, Allah has selected you and preferred you over the rest of the nations, favoured you, honoured you, and singled you out with the noblest Messenger and the most perfect Law (shar').

﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, meaning: He has not imposed on you what you cannot bear, and He has not obligated you with anything that would be burdensome for you without Allah providing you with relief and a way out. For example, the prayer, which is the greatest pillar of Islam after the two testimonies, is obligatory in full (four rak'ahs) when at home, and is shortened to two when travelling. In fear (of danger), some imams have it prayed one rak'ah, as the hadith reports. It may be prayed on foot or while riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it. Likewise, voluntary prayer while travelling may be prayed facing the qiblah or otherwise. Standing in prayer is waived by the excuse of illness, so the sick person prays sitting, and if he cannot, then lying on his side. And there are other concessions and easings in the rest of the obligatory duties and requirements. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: [In manuscript T: "peace and blessings be upon him"; in manuscripts F and A: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."] "I have been sent with the upright, tolerant religion (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah)." [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/266) from the hadith of Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him.] He also said to Mu'adh and Abu Musa when he sent them as governors to Yemen: "Give good news and do not repel; make things easy and do not make them difficult." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3038, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1732.] The hadiths on this are numerous. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas said regarding Allah's words ﴿and He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾: that means, "any narrowness."

* *

Allah's words: ﴿The religion of your father Ibrahim﴾. Ibn Jarir said: it is in the accusative because of an implied verb: "And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion," meaning, "any narrowness; rather He has made it broad for you, like the religion of your father Ibrahim." [He said: "It is also possible that it is in the accusative because of an implied verb: Adhere to the religion of your father Ibrahim."] [Addition from manuscripts T and F.]

I say: this meaning in this verse is like His words: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Ibrahim, a true monotheist﴾ [Al-An'am: 161].

As for His words: ﴿He named you Muslims before, and in this (Revelation)﴾. Imam 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan also said likewise.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾ means Ibrahim, based on His words: ﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation to You﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 128].

Ibn Jarir said: this has no basis, because it is well known that Ibrahim did not name this Ummah "Muslims" in the Qur'an, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿He named you Muslims before and in this﴾. Mujahid said: Allah named you Muslims before, in the earlier Scriptures and in the Reminder, and ﴿in this﴾ means the Qur'an. Others have said likewise.

I say: this is the correct view, because He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He has chosen you, and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, then He urged them and encouraged them to follow what the Messenger (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) brought, by telling them that it is the religion of their father Ibrahim the Friend (Khalil). Then He mentioned His favour upon this Ummah by the honour and praise attributed to it in ancient times and earliest ages, in the books of the prophets, recited to the rabbis and monks. So He said: ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that is, before this Qur'an, ﴿and in this﴾. Al-Nasa'i, when interpreting this verse, said:

Hisham ibn 'Ammar informed us: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb informed us: Mu'awiyah ibn Salam informed us that his brother Zayd ibn Salam told him, from Abu Salam, that he told him: al-Harith al-Ash'ari informed me, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever calls with the call of the Jahiliyyah, he is from the kneeling-crowds of Hell." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he fasts and prays?" He said: "Yes, even if he fasts and prays. So call with the call of Allah with which He named you: the Muslims, the Believers, the servants of Allah." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11349.]

We have already mentioned this hadith in full when interpreting His words: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may be mindful (of Him)﴾ in Surah al-Baqarah [verse 21]. And for this reason He said: ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you, and you may be witnesses over the people﴾.

That is: We have made you thus, a moderate (wasat) Ummah, just and excellent, whose justice is witnessed by all the nations, so that on the Day of Resurrection you may be ﴿witnesses over the people﴾, because all nations on that day will acknowledge its supremacy and its virtue over every other nation. Therefore their testimony against them will be accepted on the Day of Resurrection, that the Messengers delivered the message of their Lord to them, and the Messenger will testify against this Ummah that he delivered that to them. This matter has already been discussed at His words: ﴿And thus We have made you a moderate Ummah, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143], and we have mentioned the hadith of Nuh and his Ummah in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary.

* *

Allah's words: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾, meaning: receive this great blessing by giving thanks for it, fulfil Allah's right upon you by performing what He has made obligatory, obeying what He has required, and abandoning what He has forbidden. Among the most important of these is establishing prayer and giving zakah, which is kindness to Allah's creation, by what He has made obligatory: for the poor to be given by the rich a small portion of his wealth each year for the weak and the needy, as its explanation and detail has already been given in the verse on zakah in Surah "al-Tawbah" [see the commentary on verse 60 of Surah al-Tawbah].

* *

Allah's words: ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾, meaning: rely on Allah, seek His help, put your trust in Him, and be strengthened by Him. ﴿He is your Protector (mawla)﴾, meaning: your Guardian, your Helper, and the one who grants you victory over your enemies. ﴿So what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper﴾, meaning: [what an excellent] [Addition from manuscript T.] Guardian and what an excellent Helper against enemies.

Wuhayb ibn al-Ward said: Allah the Exalted says: "Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, and I will remember you when I am angry, and I will not destroy you along with those who are destroyed. And when you are wronged, be patient and be content with My help, for My help for you is better than your help for yourself." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

And Allah the Exalted knows best. To Him belong praise, favour, good commendation, and blessing. I ask Him for success and protection in all actions and words.

This is the end of the commentary on Surah "al-Hajj." May Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace, honour, and dignity, and may Allah be pleased with the Companions and those who followed them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. [In manuscript T: "and grant them abundant peace until the Day of Judgement. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."]

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed over this second prostration in Surah al-Hajj, whether prostration is prescribed in it or not, and there are two opinions. Earlier, at the first prostration, we mentioned the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Surah al-Hajj has been given two prostrations, so whoever does not prostrate for them should not recite them."

* *

Allah's words: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾, meaning with your wealth, your tongues, and your selves, as He said: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102].

* *

Allah's words: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, meaning: O this Ummah, Allah has selected you and preferred you over the rest of the nations, favoured you, honoured you, and singled you out with the noblest Messenger and the most perfect Law (shar').

﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, meaning: He has not imposed on you what you cannot bear, and He has not obligated you with anything that would be burdensome for you without Allah providing you with relief and a way out. For example, the prayer, which is the greatest pillar of Islam after the two testimonies, is obligatory in full (four rak'ahs) when at home, and is shortened to two when travelling. In fear (of danger), some imams have it prayed one rak'ah, as the hadith reports. It may be prayed on foot or while riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it. Likewise, voluntary prayer while travelling may be prayed facing the qiblah or otherwise.
